articles.title: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton: Alexander Isak continues goalscoring hot streak as Reds win at Anfield
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Liverpool move up to fourth with a 2-0 win over third-place Brighton at Anfield; Pascal Gross scored an own goal from a Florian Wirtz shot before Alexander Isak struck for a third consecutive Premier League game
articles.body:
Isak's goal, finished emphatically from Bradley Barcola's right-wing cut-back, came four first-half minutes after Pascal Gross had diverted a Florian Wirtz shot into his own net.

Brighton arrived at Anfield having scored 23 goals in their first seven games of the season but lacked a clinical edge, with Yasin Ayari blazing a golden chance over moments before the opener.

Ayari later struck the post with a curling effort from outside the box as Brighton finished the game with only one shot on target despite having 64 per cent of the possession.

Trey Nyoni, a second-half substitute for Wirtz, who went down the tunnel after taking a knock to his ankle, also made a crucial, last-ditch tackle to deny Maxim De Cuyper in the Liverpool box.

The hosts had chances to add to their lead, wasting several counter-attacks and drawing Bart Verbruggen saves from Ronald Araujo and Cody Gakpo. But their first-half flurry proved sufficient to secure a first Premier League home win under Andoni Iraola.

The result takes them above Chelsea into fourth in the Premier League, only a point behind Brighton, who taste defeat for the first time since August. Liverpool's fourth win in a row in all competitions also provides further evidence of their attack finally clicking.

Isak's goal, his sixth of the season in the Premier League, came after fine work by summer signing Barcola, who stole possession high up the pitch before driving forward and picking out his team-mate.

articles.title: Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle: Pressure rises on Pierre Sage after dreadful second-half showing
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as second-half goals from Will Osula and Harvey Barnes give Newcastle 2-0 win over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park to raise pressure on under-fire head coach Pierre Sage
articles.body:
Having been battered 5-0 by Brighton last weekend, Palace badly needed a response for their under-fire head coach but were soundly beaten by the Magpies - whose own manager Matthias Jaissle had also come into the game feeling the heat.

The manner of Palace's defeat will be of particular concern given that, after a forgettable first half, they barely re-emerged for the second with Jaissle clearly winning the battle of the half-time teamtalks. Barely a minute after the restart the hosts were behind when Jacob Murphy's excellent cross was turned home by Will Osula.

It would have been two soon after save for a tight VAR offside call against Joe Willock, who had been threaded through by a fine Joelinton pass. But Palace failed to use the let-off to their advantage and were soon punished when Harvey Barnes slammed home a second just before the hour.

That was enough for the murmurs of discontent to begin to ripple through a previously patient home support, who were shown little to give them any hope of a comeback as only Dario Osorio's long-range effort caused Lukas Hornicek any concern.

Newcastle's impressive victory lifts them seventh in the Premier League standings following a first win in three and an all-too-rare clean sheet - their first since August.

articles.summary: El meta esloveno atendió a los medios a la conclusión del 1-0 ante el Deportivo.
articles.body: Oblak atendió a los medios a la conclusión de un partido en el que volvió a ser decisivo con varias paradas de mérito. Resumen partido: "Nos ha costado mucho. No hemos estado del todo bien. Primera parte bastante mal. Segunda mejor, subimos ritmo, pero luego bajamos un poco otra vez. El Deportivo es muy buen equipo y te puede castigar. Tuvimos un poquito de suerte. Menos mal que no nos castigaron y nos llevamos los tres puntos". Plan: "Nos costaba mucho robar. No era el plan de partido. Nos ha costado físicamente, parece que no nos hemos activado desde el inicio. Muchas veces los partidos se pierden en las primeras partes. Era algo que habíamos mejorado pero hoy volvimos a bajar el ritmo. Si lo bajas es imposible. Hay que estar al 200%". Gol de Julián: "Está claro que Julián es muy importante, que marque Julián. Está dando lo máximo de sí mismo. Feliz por él. Estoy seguro que poco a poco se ganará a la gente otra vez. Es un gran jugador, ya lo ha demostrado y está claro que lo necesitamos en la mejor forma posible". El Clásico: "Me da igual el Clásico. La Liga es muy larga y hay que pensar en nosotros. No podemos perder puntos. Ellos son dos grandes equipos. Nosotros estar arriba y pelear hasta el final. Ojalá se pueda hacer".

articles.title: No. 19 Texas blows 21-point halftime lead but still does enough to beat No. 7 Ole Miss
articles.summary: Arch Manning scored two rushing touchdowns and threw for another but also had three turnovers.
articles.body:
No. 19 Texas coughed up a 21-point lead but did enough in the fourth quarter to take down No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27.

The Longhorns led 24-3 at halftime and proceeded to give up 21 straight points as Ole Miss tied the game. Arch Manning's short touchdown run with 8:04 to go put the Longhorns ahead for good before a curious tactical decision hurt Ole Miss' chances of winning the game.

But the Rebels still somehow had a shot to at least tie the game in the final minutes.

After kicking a field goal to cut Texas' lead to seven inside the final two minutes, the Rebels needed to recover an onside kick. And they did after the kick bounced off multiple players.

But without any timeouts, Ole Miss ran out of time. The Rebels got to the Texas 24-yard line, but Trinidad Chambliss' last-gasp pass was intercepted in the end zone.

After Manning gave Texas a 31-24 lead, Ole Miss started with the ball on its own 47-yard line after a late hit penalty on the ensuing kickoff return. The Rebels gained just 12 yards and faced fourth-and-10 from the Texas 41-yard line while trailing by seven.

A field goal would simply cut Texas' lead to four with just over six minutes to go. The Rebels would still need to find the end zone or kick two more field goals to take the lead. And yet, Ole Miss coach Pete Golding sent out Lucas Carneiro for a 58-yard field goal attempt.

The play clock was winding down as the strong-legged Carneiro lined up for the kick. Instead of taking a delay of game and punting — a defensible decision given the game context — Golding called his first timeout. He then kept Carneiro on the field to try to cut the lead to four.

Texas then drained nearly four minutes off the clock before Gianni Spetic's short field goal made it a two-possession lead that Ole Miss ultimately couldn't overcome.

Another uneven performance for the Texas offense

Texas is still looking to put a complete game together.

The Longhorns looked like the preseason top-five team they were billed as in the first half as they scored three straight touchdowns to build that 24-3 lead. The Longhorns were dominant in the second quarter, as Manning found Ryan Wingo for a 50-yard TD after he ran for his first score.

But Manning also turned the ball over three times. With starting left tackle Trevor Goosby carted off in the first half and unavailable, Manning fumbled on the first drive of the third quarter after instant pressure off the left side. That fumble was recovered by Kam Franklin in the end zone for an Ole Miss touchdown.

Texas then punted three straight times as Ole Miss tied the game and Manning threw his second pick of the game on a horrible decision into triple coverage early in the fourth quarter.

It was a play that could have been costly. Instead, the Texas defense quickly forced a punt, and the Longhorns drove 80 yards in six plays for Manning's go-ahead touchdown.

That drive was powered by running back Raleek Brown, who shouldered much of the rushing workload with Hollywood Smothers sidelined by a shoulder injury. Brown finished the game with 23 carries for 157 yards.

There are still five weeks of the regular season to go. But if the season ended today, Georgia would face Kentucky in the SEC championship game.

The Bulldogs and Wildcats are the only two teams in the SEC with just one conference loss through Week 8. Thanks to Texas' win, eight teams currently have two league losses, while another four have three losses.

Georgia and Kentucky don't play each other in 2026, though both have three ranked teams still remaining on their conference schedules. We're confident in saying that one or both of the league's title game participants is going to have two conference losses.

We have no idea who those teams will be, however. Though one thing is for certain: tiebreakers are going to be in play.

articles.title: Rodri, de deseo blanco a líder culé
articles.standfirst: Rechazó en verano al bloque de Mourinho para firmar por el conjunto culé
articles.summary: Rechazó en verano al bloque de Mourinho para firmar por el conjunto culé
articles.body: Uno de los grandes nombres propios del pasado mercado de verano fue el de Rodri. Cuando surgió la posibilidad de que el centrocampista abandonara el Manchester City, tanto el Real Madrid como el Barcelona dieron un paso al frente. El conjunto blanco necesitaba reforzar su medular y el equipo azulgrana, por su parte, aunque parecía tener bien cubierta esa demarcación sobre el papel, no quería dejar escapar la oportunidad de incorporar a uno de los mejores centrocampistas del mundo. El Real Madrid apostó con fuerza por su fichaje. Mantuvieron varios contactos con el jugador para tratar de convencerlo de que su futuro debía pasar por el Bernabéu. Incluso Mourinho intervino para intentar inclinar la balanza a favor del conjunto blanco. La operación se convirtió así en uno de los grandes focos de atención del mercado estival. Sin embargo, Rodri terminó decantándose por el Barcelona. El internacional explicó que su decisión respondía fundamentalmente a cuestiones futbolísticas: dónde podía seguir creciendo como jugador, qué proyecto le ofrecía mayores posibilidades de desarrollo, la posibilidad de liderar a un vestuario con una importante presencia de jóvenes... La decisión estuvo vinculada, por encima de todo, a su visión del proyecto deportivo. Ahora, dos meses después de aquella elección y de su llegada al conjunto azulgrana, el centrocampista se prepara para reencontrarse con el equipo al que rechazó durante el verano. En el Barcelona, Rodri se ha convertido en un futbolista imprescindible, en un líder. Ha sido titular en ocho de los nueve últimos compromisos del conjunto azulgrana. Y resulta especialmente llamativo que su única suplencia en ese periodo se produjera contra el PSG el martes, precisamente en el último compromiso que ha perdido el conjunto de Flick. Rodri saltó al terreno de juego durante la última media hora. Rodri ofrece salida de balón, facilita la circulación y ayuda a controlar los tiempos del partido. Su tándem con Pedri permite al conjunto azulgrana presumir de tener uno de los mejores centros del campo del mundo.

articles.title: The non-football fan who snapped the game beautifully
articles.summary: Peter Robinson has been a photographer at 13 FIFA World Cups since 1970.
articles.body:
You might think a man who captured images at 13 World Cups and worked as FIFA's official photographer for two decades must be passionate about football.

But Peter Robinson, who has photographed icons such as Diego Maradona, Lionel Messi, Pele and Franz Beckenbauer, admits he has never been a huge fan of the sport itself.

Robinson, 82, has travelled to competitions in close to 100 countries in a career he describes as "bonkers".

His work is now being celebrated in an exhibition that highlights its focus on the stories of football off the field, photos which curator Hugo Worthy said "tell you a huge amount about football but about life more broadly".

Robinson, who now lives in Rutland, said he believed it was his lack of "fan energy" about football that allowed him to capture unique pictures of the sport.

"It's helped me produce different images than the usual sports football photographer," Robinson explained to the BBC.

"Because their remit, their shopping lists are the things that are important in the game - goals and incidents.

"I'm destined to shoot these pictures because other people are not.

"All of the pictures have got a question mark on it for me - why did this happen like this?"

Robinson's photography journey started in the 1960s when, while booking local bands to play in Leicester, he met a group called The Contacts, made up of photography students at the Leicester School of Art, now De Montfort University.

He said they had "a good vibe" and he wondered what it would be like to make a living taking photos.

Robinson, who lived in New Parks in Leicester at the time, decided to speak to the course leader even though he did not have a camera or any photographs to show.

He chose to study photography at the school in 1964 and instantly took to it.

"It took me a day to figure out this is what I wanted to do for the rest of my life," Robinson said.

"You could shoot, and you've made the prints, and then you critique them in class.

"I felt like I was Jack the Lad. People were talking about what I had done in class and I just took to this perfectly."

While a student, Robinson admits the "last thing I wanted to do" was shoot football pictures.

However as he was "skint", he took a role delivering papers for local publication Football League Review before eventually becoming a photographer there.

Through his work with the magazine, Robinson was then asked to photograph for FIFA at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, providing pictures for the official report.

He went on to become the football body's official photographer up to the 1994 World Cup and says one of his favourite photos showed Italian captain Franco Baresi receiving a runners-up medal after that tournament's final against Brazil in Los Angeles.

The day before, Robinson scouted out the spot and decided he would need to use a flash gun to improve the lighting for the photo and "fill in" the shadows which he said would have been "horrendous" during the day.

In the corner of the shot is the World Cup trophy just out of reach of Baresi - whose Italy side lost on penalties to Brazil.

Robinson said he remembered waiting and waiting for the right moment for the shot as Baresi walked up to accept his medal.

"As I write in the caption, it's a bit like a noose for execution," he said.

"He doesn't want the lousy medal, he just wants to fall into a hole in the ground.

"And I took one photograph, that's all I took."

Another classic shot taken in October 1970 features "two bobbies" - England legend Sir Bobby Charlton preparing to take a corner while a policeman keeps an eye on supporters.

"You can see the kids in the front row of that picture. They are looking at somebody almost like he [Charlton] is a deity," Robinson said.

"Michael Palin kindly did the intro for my book and talked about how it was some kind of renaissance photo."

Earlier this year, Robinson came out of retirement to take photos at the Argentina v Cape Verde game in Miami during the 2026 World Cup.

But back in 1986, when Maradona lifted the trophy, he was also there to shoot it.

"Unlike the picture of Baresi in LA, I did not set anything up because I tried to find out where the presentation would take place and nobody seemed to be organised," Robinson said.

"I did not know whether it was going to be presented by X or Y. So I couldn't decide.

"I think I turned into the VIPs and they seemed a bit confused about who was going to do what. I think I saw that and took the picture.

"I thought it was interesting they hadn't figured out beforehand what they were going to do as regards to the presentation.

"If you look at him, he is not doing a dance he is sort of thinking 'this is what it is all about, I am with the big boys now'.

"Once he got down on the field he went back to his normal self after he got the cup.

"It just doesn't look like somebody who is going to get this accolade and that's why I like the picture, because of his body language."

His career has taken him to far-flung corners of the globe, including Madagascar.

While working for cigarette company Camel, he shot a photo of villagers playing football on a makeshift pitch during the 1987 Camel Trophy.

"Camel sponsored an off-road event that was Land Rovers and this was a thousand miles from the north of Madagascar to the south in all sorts of places," Robinson said.

"It was to photograph people driving through the jungle in Land Rovers and we flew into this village, it wasn't a straight line trip, it was jerky, they did 500 kilometres in one place and then flew by helicopter to another place.

"I had stopped in this town and I was wondering around like I do normally and came across these guys playing football.

"I was there five minutes, I saw that picture with the keeper standing there in the grass."

The exhibition at New Parks Library, on the same street as his childhood home, is showcasing 40 of his photographs.

Reflecting on his journey from Leicester to stadiums around the world, he said: "It means that it doesn't matter where you are from, you can do it, can't you?

"I come from here, it's ordinary. I like that, I like being ordinary."

Hugo Worthy said curating the exhibition had allowed him to showcase images that "tell stories that absolutely go beyond football".

"I find Peter's vision super exciting, super refreshing," he said.

"If you go through his work there is lots of action shots there, but it is not necessarily what excited me most about his work.

"He uses football as a way to talk about the human condition.

"It is a really powerful way of looking at the world through his lens of football.

"There is a really profound sense of seriousness around the way he takes pictures."

Robinson was honoured in 2025 with a lifetime achievement in sports award at the Lucie Awards, an international event celebrating "the most influential figures in contemporary photography".

Worthy said a picture of ashes being interred on the pitch at a non-league game stood out to him as one that "captures Peter's vision".

"It is about football as religion, football as this amazing focus for community, family and society," he said.

"It is this really beautiful, intimate photograph."

Robinson hopes one day his archive will be on display at De Montfort University to bring his life's story "full circle".

"I like images that have got a story and ordinary images about ordinary people," he said.

The exhibition at New Parks Library is due to run until March.

articles.title: What have Manchester United changed to turn around their WSL form?
articles.summary: It's a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month - so what have they changed to turn around their WSL form?
articles.body:
It is a different picture at Manchester United now than it was last month as they gear up for the derby against Women's Super League leaders Manchester City.

Eva Olid's side were without a win and low on confidence after their opening three matches in a disappointing start to the season.

But after getting their first win on the board against Sheffield United in the Women's League Cup, United have won six successive matches in all competitions.

They now sit fifth in the table, eight points off unbeaten rivals City, who they face on Sunday (18:00 GMT) hoping to continue their positive form.

So what has changed at United to overturn their fortunes?

Listen to BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra commentary and follow live text updates on the BBC Sport website

The most noticeable changes have happened on the pitch as new manager Olid, who joined in the summer, conceded her side needed to revert to old ways.

They were struggling to adapt to her new style which demands lots of possession, an attacking mindset and high-risk football.

They struggled in defeats by London City Lionesses and Chelsea, having just two shots on target and less than 40% possession in both matches.

Olid felt her team were trying to do too much and had lost sight of some of their strengths, including their defensive organisation.

She urged her players to revert to what they knew before their 1-1 draw with Arsenal, which showed signs of improvement.

"The things they were good at before, they need to keep and at the same time, little by little, we need to implement our new style," Olid said before that game.

"It's trying to find this balance. Maybe they thought I would expect them to do everything in the first match but that is impossible. You need time."

That draw at Emirates Stadium was the catalyst for change at United, offering a foundation to build upon.

They had a tough start but then had a run of games against lower-ranked opposition, and two successive WSL matches at home.

The difference from their first three WSL games and their next three was stark.

They won the maximum nine points, scored six goals, conceded just two and almost doubled their possession percentage.

By returning to a more familiar defensive structure and adding in elements of Olid's new style, they began to cause more problems up front too.

Having had just 197 passes ending in the final third in their first three games, they recorded a combined 529 against West Ham, Liverpool and Charlton Athletic.

They quadrupled the number of shots they took too, going from 10 to 42 and won more duels in the air.

Perhaps the biggest changes at United have been off the pitch.

Olid explained that her side had navigated a "transitional period" and had taken part in big discussions following their 5-0 drubbing by Chelsea.

Players needed to find confidence and Olid admitted the "honest conversations" had to come up with a solution.

"The first two games were good learning for us to connect as a team and for me to know what the players needed from me," said Olid. "The players also know what I needed. It was about trying to find that balance.

"I feel now we are connected. That doesn't mean we won't have more [of those] less good days, but I think we have that understanding of each other."

Their form at the start of the season impacted individuals with vice-captain Ella Toone missing out on England selection for the first time under Sarina Wiegman.

She responded by scoring in their 3-1 win at Charlton on Sunday, while summer signing Andrea Medina has grown to become a crucial member of the squad.

The international break proved to be a valuable time for Olid to readjust to her new role, reflect on what needed to change and to spend time on the training pitch.

England defender and United captain Maya le Tissier was among those to return with renewed energy having impressed for her country during the break.

The backroom staff positions were also confirmed and Olid has been able to build a group she hopes can lead United to success going forward.

Fellow Spaniard Jose Herrera joined as assistant coach, alongside Gavin Beith, who worked with Olid at former club Hearts.

Speaking about the international break, Olid said: "I had time to re-organise everything, the roles for the new staff and how we are going to work together.

"This break, for me, was amazing. It was like a new start. It was about keeping the good energy from the last matches but then having a new start."

Now, having been on a winning run, Olid hopes the proposition of a Manchester derby on Sunday will prove to be added motivation for her players.

"I always think that before big games, you want to give confidence to the players and at the same time, you try to motivate them with the opposition," she told BBC.

"It's a derby. I think the players are always motivated, but against City, there has to be something else, no?"

articles.title: Neymar, tras su expulsión: "Le di la oportunidad a un idiota de hacerse notar"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño vio la roja por taparse la boca al hablar con Rodrigo Nestor, del Bahía: "Es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella"
articles.summary: El brasileño vio la roja por taparse la boca al hablar con Rodrigo Nestor, del Bahía: "Es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella"
articles.body: Neymar habló después del partido entre el Santos y el Bahía donde fue expulsado por taparse la boca cuando se dirigía a Rodrigo Nestor. El brasileño fue muy crítico con el jugador rival y pidió disculpas a su afición. "No soy muy de hablar sobre lo que pasa en el partido, pero lo que hizo Nestor conmigo es muy grave. Grave porque es una ley creada contra el racismo, y él quiso aprovecharse de ella", comentó en su Instagram. "Estoy muy triste, porque él fue muy safado (deshonesto). Muy safado, de verdad. Dijo en la entrevista que no podía repetir lo que yo dije, porque hay niños viendo... Hermano, él simuló. Yo tiré el balón a su cintura y él se llevó la mano a la cara. ¿Qué ejemplo quiere dar? Habló de educación... Hermano, yo también tengo educación. Y otra cosa: yo soy hombre", comentaba Neymar. "Lo que hiciste no se hace. Y quien creó esa ley, cuidado. Porque puede haber safadeza (desfachatez) y pasar lo que me pasó a mí. Hice una mierda, ¿no? Le di oportunidad a un idiota de hacerse notar. Gracias, Nestor, yo voy a dormir con la conciencia tranquila. Tú, con tu safadeza, no vas a dormir tranquilo, no. No vas a dormir tranquilo, no!", concluyó.

articles.summary: Partidazo en Anoeta entre dos equipos al alza
articles.body: La Real Sociedad recibirá esta tarde al Levante en Anoeta con la intención de sumar su cuarta victoria seguida en LaLiga y mantenerse en los puestos europeos, a los que soñarán con acercarse los granotas, algo que podrían hacer si dan continuidad al triunfo del miércoles contra el Athletic y se llevan los tres puntos. Ambos equipos están protagonizando partidos con goles, así que todo apunta a tarde entretenida. El partido entre Real Sociedad y Levante de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se juega el domingo 25 de octubre a las 18:30 horas. El partido entre Real Sociedad y Levante de la jornada 10 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través del canal DAZN LaLiga. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles. La Real Sociedad llega tras haber sumado tres victorias consecutivas en LaLiga EA Sports, la última ante el Málaga por 2-5 en el Estadio La Rosaleda. El Levante llega tras haber ganado al Athletic Club entre semana. Era el partido aplazado de la jornada 6 y los granotas se llevaron los tres puntos ganando 3-1 a los rojiblancos.

articles.title: Mourinho contra el mejor Barça de la historia: tres años de guerra en 17 batallas
articles.standfirst: De la goleada del 5-0 al dedo en el ojo de Tito Vilanova, del “¿por qué?” al “calma” de Cristiano: la crónica de la rivalidad más tensa que ha vivido el fútbol español, cuando el portugués se midió al Barça de Guardiola
articles.summary: De la goleada del 5-0 al dedo en el ojo de Tito Vilanova, del “¿por qué?” al “calma” de Cristiano: la crónica de la rivalidad más tensa que ha vivido el fútbol español, cuando el portugués se midió al Barça de Guardiola
articles.body: Pocas veces el fútbol ha sido tan parecido a una trinchera. Entre noviembre de 2010 y marzo de 2013, José Mourinho y el Barcelona libraron 17 Clásicos que no se jugaban solo en el césped, sino en las salas de prensa, en los despachos de la UEFA y en el imaginario de dos aficiones que aprendieron a tenerse manía con método. Enfrente tenía el portugués a uno de los mejores equipos que ha pisado un campo en este siglo, aquel Barça de Guardiola. Mourinho no vino a admirarlo; vino a derribarlo, y para ello estaba dispuesto a ensuciarse las manos. El prólogo lo había escrito él mismo meses antes, cuando su Inter eliminó a ese Barça en una semifinal de Champions y celebró el pase corriendo bajo los aspersores del Camp Nou. Aquella carrera fue su carta de presentación en una ciudad que ya conocía: Mourinho había sido allí traductor y ayudante de Robson y Van Gaal en los noventa, un segundo de a bordo que volvía convertido en almirante del enemigo. El primer acto fue una bofetada. El 29 de noviembre de 2010, en su estreno como visitante en el Camp Nou, el Madrid encajó un 5-0 que todavía duele en Concha Espina. Mourinho, que jamás en su carrera había recibido cinco goles, salió a la sala de prensa sin esconderse: “Es una derrota muy fácil de digerir. Premia a un equipo que jugó muy bien y castiga a otro que jugó muy mal”. Piqué despidió a los blancos enseñando los cinco dedos de la manita. Fue la última vez que el portugués aceptó una derrota con deportividad. A partir de ahí, cambió de armas. La primavera de 2011 marcó un antes y un después. En apenas dieciocho días, Madrid y Barça se vieron cuatro veces: Liga, final de Copa y la ida y vuelta de las semifinales de Champions. El Madrid rescató la Copa en Mestalla, con un cabezazo de Cristiano en la prórroga que rompió una sequía de dieciocho años, pero el fútbol pronto quedó sepultado bajo la pólvora dialéctica. En la previa de la Champions, Guardiola, harto, estalló con una frase que resume una época: “En esta sala, él es el puto jefe, el puto amo. Fuera del campo ya me ha ganado. No quiero competir ni un instante”. Uno de los técnicos más elegante del mundo bajaba al barro al que Mourinho lo había arrastrado. Después vino el monólogo más célebre de la carrera del portugués. Tras caer 0-2 en el Bernabéu, con Pepe expulsado y él mismo enviado a la grada, Mourinho convirtió la rueda de prensa en un juicio sumarísimo: “¿Por qué? ¿Por qué? ¿Por qué?”, repitió, antes de enumerar árbitros como quien recita una lista negra y de dejar una sentencia envenenada: “Guardiola es un fantástico entrenador, pero ha ganado una Champions que a mí me daría vergüenza ganar”. La UEFA lo sancionó con cinco partidos. El Barça pasó a Wembley y levantó la Orejona. Mourinho había perdido la batalla deportiva, pero había plantado una semilla de sospecha que germinaría durante años. En la Supercopa de agosto de 2011, una tangana en el descuento del Camp Nou terminó con la imagen que lo persigue para siempre: Mourinho acercándose por la espalda al banquillo rival y metiéndole el dedo en el ojo a Tito Vilanova, el segundo de Guardiola. Interrogado después, no solo negó la agresión, sino que humilló a su víctima: “¿Pito Vilanova? No sé quién es ese Pito”. Piqué resumió el sentir de media España: “Mourinho está destrozando el fútbol español”. El dedo en el ojo fue mucho más que un gesto, fue el símbolo de una rivalidad que había perdido los frenos. Y sin embargo, en mitad del fango, germinó el fútbol. La temporada 2011-12 trajo el Clásico más importante de aquellos tres años. El 21 de abril de 2012, en un Camp Nou abarrotado, Cristiano recibió de Ozil, batió a Valdés y mandó callar a noventa mil almas con las palmas hacia abajo: “Calma”. Aquel 1-2 encarriló la única Liga que el Madrid le arrebató a aquel Barça, un título de récord con cien puntos que puso fin a la hegemonía culé. Seis días después, agotado, Guardiola anunció que se marchaba. Mourinho había conseguido su propósito: desgastar al coloso hasta que el coloso dijo basta. El tercer acto fue la redención, aunque con sabor agridulce. Con Guardiola fuera y un Tito Vilanova que pronto tendría que ausentarse para tratarse un cáncer, la balanza se inclinó por fin del lado blanco. Mourinho ganó la Supercopa de 2012 y, ya en 2013, eliminó al Barça en las semifinales de Copa con un contundente 1-3 en el Camp Nou. Cerró su serie particular con cinco Clásicos seguidos sin perder, como si el tiempo quisiera concederle una tregua antes de la despedida. El portugués, que había empezado recibiendo cinco goles, se iba dándole lecciones a su verdugo. El balance de aquellos tres años es un empate técnico que esconde una guerra total: cinco victorias, seis empates y seis derrotas. Pero reducir aquello a números sería traicionar su esencia. Mourinho no transformó solo un marcador. Transformó la manera de entender el Clásico, lo convirtió en un campo de batalla psicológico del que el fútbol español tardó años en recuperarse. Quien quiera entender el Clásico de hoy, con sus mosaicos, sus pancartas y sus recelos arbitrales, haría bien en mirar atrás. Allí, en aquellas diecisiete batallas, está el origen de casi todo.

articles.title: 75 veces al rescate
articles.standfirst: Lunin cumple su efemérides en el Madrid siempre de urgencia en sus siete años de blanco
articles.summary: Lunin cumple su efemérides en el Madrid siempre de urgencia en sus siete años de blanco
articles.body: En los matrimonios cumplir 75 años es la Boda de Brillantes; en el caso de Andriy Lunin, que se casó en chándal, más le vale brillar porque es la 75ª vez que acude al rescate de la portería blanca de urgencia, siempre resguardada por Courtois, sobre el que no hay debate. Siempre se le requiere de un día para otro, vive en un susto permanente. Habitual bombero en el Madrid, aterriza de nuevo sin un solo minuto esta temporada ni en Liga ni en Champions. Su último partido en Liga fue en ante el Espanyol en mayo aunque había vuelto a la titularidad contra el Atleti también por lesión del belga. Y la última en Champions en abril en la derrota 4-3 en Múnich, hace casi medio año. No tiene partidos pequeños el chico. Eso sí todos los aficionados blancos recuerdan su memorable temporada en 2024, llevando en volandas al equipo hasta la decimoquinta contra el Dortmund en Wembley, con grandes actuaciones ante City (con tanda de penaltis para la historia) o Bayern. Luego en la de 2026 no anduvo tan fino también contra el equipo muniqués. En los 74 anteriores ha recibido 91 goles (23 partidos imbatido), 3 amarillas y 1 roja en todas las competiciones. En este Real Madrid del regreso de Mourinho, Lunin ha arrancado su séptima temporada a la sombra de Courtois. El belga, que se cae esta noche por una gripe inoportuna, ya forma parte de la historia de la portería blanca. Para muchos, el guardameta más grande de la historia del club, por encima de Casillas, Zamora, Araquistain... Un dominio de su puesto que no admite debate alguno y que apenas encuentra puntos débiles en su primera temporada en la Casa Blanca: en la 2018-19. El portero ucraniano, después de un par de años de cesiones, se instaló en la primera plantilla del Madrid en el verano de 2020, el de la pandemia. A esas alturas, Courtois ya era intocable para Zidane. Como luego lo fue para Ancelotti, Xabi Alonso, Arbeloa y, ahora, Mourinho. En ese recorrido de portero suplente de largo aliento apareció un oasis: la temporada 2023-24. La grave lesión de rodilla que sufrió Courtois a las puertas de LaLiga llevó al club a fichar a Kepa. Parecía una condena a otra suplencia para el ucraniano. Sin embargo, tras la Supercopa de España, Lunin se convirtió en el titular y en el héroe del Madrid en la tanda de penaltis del Etihad. Eso sí, en cuanto Courtois estuvo listo para regresar, Ancelotti volvió a darle las llaves de la portería. Suya fue la final de la Champions en Wembley. Lunin afronta la temporada con el mismo papel de las anteriores: a la sombra de Courtois y a la espera de que Mourinho le conceda oportunidades en la Copa más allá de la de esta noche. La temporada pasada apenas disputó el partido de Albacete hasta que las lesiones se cruzaron en el camino del guardameta belga y le abrieron las puertas de la titularidad. Así, el portero de Krasnohrad sumó seis apariciones en LaLiga. La falta de minutos en el Real Madrid ha provocado que Lunin desaparezca de las convocatorias de la selección ucraniana. No porque la titularidad de Trubin, el guardameta del Benfica, sea intocable, sino porque Ucrania no cuenta con el portero de Krasnohrad desde junio de 2025. Y se trata de una situación que, por ahora, parece no tener fácil solución. A la espera de aumentar su número de partidos con el Real Madrid, Lunin suma 74 encuentros defendiendo la portería blanca en las seis temporadas que lleva en el club. En ese recorrido ha conquistado once títulos, entre ellos dos Ligas de Campeones. Un currículo de gran nivel, muy por encima del que han firmado otros guardametas suplentes en la historia de la entidad de Chamartín.

articles.title: Uli Hoeneß: Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern than at Liverpool
articles.summary: Uli Hoeneß believes Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern Munich than he currently does at Liverpool.The Bayern honorary president made the remar...
articles.body:
Uli Hoeneß believes Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern Munich than he currently does at Liverpool .

The Bayern honorary president made the remarks in an interview with German newspaper Welt am Sonntag.

Wirtz made his name at Bayer Leverkusen before moving to Anfield, in a then-British record deal worth up to £116m. He arrived in England as a back-to-back winner of the Bundesliga 's Player of the Season award, but the 23-year-old has not hit the heights expected.

Hoeneß has been keeping a close eye on the German's fortunes and his verdict is that the problem lies in how Liverpool have used him.

Hoeneß contrasted Wirtz's central role at Leverkusen with his standing in the Liverpool side, suggesting he has lost the influence that made him stand out in the Bundesliga.

Bayern Munich had been interested in signing Wirtz prior to his Premier League transfer, and Hoeneß is confident the environment at the Allianz Arena would suit the midfielder more.

Hoeneß questions Liverpool's use of Wirtz: "In Leverkusen, he got every ball"

"Florian Wirtz would play much better for Bayern than he does at Liverpool," Hoeneß told Welt am Sonntag .

"I watch a lot of his games. They haven't integrated him properly at all. In Leverkusen, he got every ball; in Liverpool, he's just one among many."

Wirtz has faced scrutiny after a slow start to his second season at Liverpool, and was singled out after the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month.

However, he has shown glimpses of improvement in recent games. The Germany international has recorded goal involvements in each of his last three appearances, and opened his goal account against Villarreal in midweek.

Liverpool take on Brighton in the Premier League this afternoon, with Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler discussing Wirtz ahead of the game. He said the Seagulls must stop Wirtz's impact as a collective, highlighting his ability in one-vs-one situations.

articles.title: Barcelona revive interest in €30m-rated Juventus defender; move dependent on Alejandro Balde – report
articles.summary: Barcelona made quite a few signings during the summer transfer window, bringing in the likes of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Rodri and Joao Cancelo.One oth...
articles.body:
Barcelona made quite a few signings during the summer transfer window, bringing in the likes of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Rodri and Joao Cancelo.

One other player the Catalan club were interested in but eventually did not move for was Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso.

Now, according to Calciomercato (h/t FCB World ), Barça have renewed their interest in the versatile full-back.

The Catalans are monitoring the Italy international, who could become a serious option if someone like Alejandro Balde leaves Hansi Flick's squad.

Juventus set €30 million asking price for Cambiaso

The Italian giants value Cambiaso at around €30 million, with the defender under contract until June 2029.

His ability to operate on either flank makes him an attractive option for Barcelona, particularly given Flick's preference for versatile defenders comfortable in possession.

Andrea Cambiaso is a fullback on Barcelona's radar. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images)

Cambiaso has endured a difficult start to the new season, suffering from an ankle problem that has limited his involvement at Juventus.

Meanwhile, Barça potentially making a move for Cambiaso could depend directly on the future of out-of-favour Alejandro Balde.

Roma are considering a January loan move for the Spaniard with an option to buy, while Juventus have also previously shown interest in his services.

That said, there have been no formal negotiations between the two clubs so far for either full-back.

Would Cambiaso be a sensible replacement for Balde?

Cambiaso's versatility is the most exciting aspect of his profile, and he could provide squad depth on both flanks.

His attacking instincts and willingness to advance into forward areas, whether overlapping or inverting into midfield, would suit Barça 's approach.

Nevertheless, spending €30 million on another full-back would be justified only if Barça managed to recoup a similar amount or more from a sale like Balde's.

Hansi Flick already has Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart, who can play on both flanks, and should not add another name for the sake of it.

Barcelona need to make a decision on the development of Alejandro Balde. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

Balde's situation is equally serious . Although the academy graduate has struggled for minutes, he remains a young player with considerable pace and attacking potential.

Allowing him to leave on loan without a purchase option would be a much better option than parting ways with him permanently.

Barça should therefore assess whether signing Cambiaso would genuinely improve the squad or if they would be better off trusting Balde.

It remains to be seen how Cambiaso recovers from his ankle problem and whether Barcelona make a move for him in the near future.

articles.title: Australia reach World Cup semis & New Zealand get back on track
articles.summary: Australia edge to a 36-22 victory in a pulsating Group A match against Fiji to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.
articles.body:
Australia edged to a 36-22 victory in a pulsating match against Fiji to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Having lost their previous five meetings against Australia by an aggregate score of 246-16, a stunned Brisbane crowd watched Fiji enjoy territorial advantage in the first half and take a 16-12 lead after the break.

However, the momentum switched back to Kevin Walters' side in a crucial 60-second spell.

Solomone Saukuru raced in to seemingly put Fiji 20-12 ahead - but when it was ruled out for obstruction, Australia immediately went up the other end and Tom Trbojevic scored to bring the teams level.

Trbojevic, who looked vulnerable in defence, crossed twice more for Australia and Jacob Preston added a further try after Semi Valemei had completed his hat-trick for Fiji.

"There are definitely some areas to improve on," Trbojevic told Premier Sports. "We didn't start as we wanted to and couldn't get a flow. We just needed to play our style of footy.

"We weren't at our best but we came away with two points. We need to improve. We've got to enjoy a win but we've got to be our harshest critics too."

Brisbane Broncos centre Kotoni Staggs had opened the scoring for Australia on his home ground, while Sam Walker capped his debut with a try and 12 points with the boot.

But the manner in which their pack were outmuscled - and in which they allowed Taane Milne and Valemei to score - will be a concern for Walters, whose team head into the last four despite delivering two unconvincing performances in beating New Zealand and Fiji.

New Zealand will take on Fiji in a make-or-break final pool game on Saturday, 31 October (04:30 GMT), having overcome an early scare themselves in their 82-16 victory over the Cook Islands in Christchurch.

Jamayne Isaako, who is joining Melbourne Storm next term, took the headlines as he scored a record 38 points for the Kiwis.

It was the perfect way for Stacey Jones' team to bounce back from their 24-22 opening Group A defeat by Australia but it did not go entirely to script, as the Cook Islands recovered from 12-0 down to lead 16-12.

With two-time World Cup winner Valentine Holmes in their ranks, Karmichael Hunt's team responded superbly as Esom Ioka grabbed a hat-trick of tries in response to early efforts from Isaako and Ronaldo Mulitalo.

However, from there it was one-way traffic as the Kiwis took control to lead 36-16 by the break.

Isaako crossed three times overall, while Test debutant Tanner Stowers-Smith, Mulitalo and Casey McLean each scored twice.

Scott Sorensen, Kodi Nikorima, Te Maire Martin, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad and Keano Kini, who replaced injured star full-back Kalyn Ponga in the New Zealand line-up, also claimed tries.

Isaako's points haul - which included 13 conversions - eclipsed Tasesa Lavea's previous mark of 32 points in a single game, which was recorded against the same opposition in 2000.

Kiwi Ferns roll towards Samoa or England clash

New Zealand's women had earlier thrashed France 92-0 in the same stadium, with Apii Nicholls scoring four tries.

Stacey Waaka and Mele Hufanga both claimed a hat-trick of tries in a dominant performance by the co-hosts.

Mackenzie Wiki, Raecene McGregor and Tenika Willison all crossed twice with Chantay Kiria-Ratu and Kaiyah Atai also going over in an 18-try demolition job.

The Kiwi Ferns have now defeated France by a combined score of 236-0 across three World Cup encounters.

New Zealand, who defeated Fiji 18-12 in the their opening match, will round off their Pool B campaign against Papua New Guinea on Saturday, 31 October (06:45 GMT).

Ricky Henry's side look set to face either Samoa or England in the semi-finals of the competition.

Fiji face France in the other remaining group match on Saturday, 31 October (02:20 GMT).

articles.title: Cesc Fabregas hails Como’s squad depth as they follow up historic Man Utd clash with crucial Sassuolo win
articles.summary: Cesc Fabregas has lauded the growing maturity of his Como side after they successfully navigated a grueling schedule to secure a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo...
articles.body:
Cesc Fabregas has lauded the growing maturity of his Como side after they successfully navigated a grueling schedule to secure a 2-0 victory against Sassuolo. Following their historic European exploits against Manchester United, the Italian outfit proved they have the depth to compete on multiple fronts.

Como continued their impressive run of form on Saturday, securing a third consecutive victory with a professional 2-0 win over Sassuolo. A brace from Tasos Douvikas was enough to seal the points, but the real story for Fabregas was his team's ability to maintain high energy levels despite a congested fixture list that recently included a high-profile Champions League encounter with Manchester United .

"It depends. Every time is a bit different, today certainly it was more the physical aspect, the games against Manchester United and Fiorentina before took energy away from us," Fabregas explained, as quoted by TUTTOmercatoWEB . "Coming to compete here... it mattered to arrive with energy. With people who had been waiting for weeks or months to find space. The real challenge of this season is the close games. The biggest teams, if you see, are in difficulty with so many changes."

The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder emphasized the importance of his fringe players stepping up when called upon. "The other team instead arrives after 8 days of preparing for the match. Victory gives you extra strength, even better to win in this way. Today Kambwala played, Ricci, Lahdo made his debut. Having everyone available and giving a hand until the end of the season is a good thing," he added.

Greek forward Douvikas was the undisputed star of the show, and Fabregas was quick to point out the immense work rate behind the striker's clinical finishing. The Spaniard believes Douvikas has all the attributes required to become one of the most feared center-forwards in the division if he continues his current trajectory of development.

"Tasos wants you to give him information. He always wants to talk, he is a guy who always wants to improve, he is scoring goals... I know how much work is behind it. He is growing in a way that could make him become a very, very important center-forward. He trains at a thousand, he is a very generous guy, in this sense we are very happy. In these last three years, he has been one of those signings that has given satisfaction," he noted.

Beyond the attacking displays, Como's defensive resilience caught the eye as they kept a clean sheet despite fielding a brand-new backline. Fabregas noted that the team is becoming more adept at managing different phases of the game, a skill they have refined even since their testing night against Manchester United at Old Trafford.

"I am very happy with this. When a team defends well it is always better than attacking. We must gain confidence. Even after Manchester United it seems that the team is managing some aspects to improve better. If you look at the defense today it is the first time they have all played together. Plus Ricci in front of them. We cannot forget this and I don't. There is work behind it. The guys understand what can be improved and try to make it available," he explained.

Fabregas also touched upon the necessity of managing stars like Nico Paz, who was rested following a heavy international and European workload. The manager insisted that rotation is a non-negotiable part of the process for a young team trying to establish themselves as a force in both domestic and continental competitions.

"I think it's a great challenge, especially after the Champions League. Coming here with so many changes and this performance, especially in the second half. We didn't leave anything to them, to play or have opportunities. There are moments during the season that we have to manage like this. This is a process of adaptation, we are very young and for me today the reaction was important. I liked the team very much," Fabregas concluded.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Manchester United captain dropped for crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick's tactics after Man Utd's heavy defeat to Como on Wednesday; club captain dropped from squad for Sunday's Premier League game at home to Bournemouth, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The captain was named on the bench after he criticised Michael Carrick's tactics following Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

He was an unused subsititute in the defeat, with Joshua Zirkzee and Shea Lacey preferred as options from the bench.

"Picking the team is always a difficult decision," Carrick told Sky Sports . "We've got to make what we feel is the right one for the team to try to get the performance we want."

Carrick described his reasons for dropping his captain as "pure football."

Sky Sports News reported on Thursday that Sunday's game against the Cherries could be pivotal for Carrick , who is under heavy pressure amid United's dreadful start to the season.

But Carrick's side were without their captain for the 3-0 loss, who told TNT Sports after the loss to Como: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

Asked if the tactics were to blame for the defeat, Fernandes replied: "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me.

"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."

Sky Sports News reported on Thursday Fernandes would not be stripped of the captaincy for his comments.

But at his pre-match press conference on Friday - which he unusually began with an emotional monologue - Carrick refused to rule out disciplinary measures being taken against Fernandes.

"The most important thing for me is the team and the dynamics in the squad. It is about the football club. Whatever the situation is, I will always do what is best for the football club," he said.

"If I've spoken to him or haven't... this isn't the time to go into details."

Fernandes was the second United player to publicly criticise the club this month after Lisandro Martinez's comments following the Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid.

Martinez said: "I expect more from our technical director [director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Martinez was not dropped for United's following game, playing 45 minutes of the 1-1 draw at Leeds - but was also benched for the visit of Bournemouth.

Neville: Fernandes comments were devastating

Speaking amid the news of Fernandes' benching, Gary Neville called Manchester United's dressing room "toxic" and said the club's players have been a "wrecking ball" towards managers.

He told Sky Sports News : "For the captain to come out and speak like he did, we're probably only getting one or two per cent of what he actually thinks. Imagine what they're saying in there. It will be toxic.

"The two most prominent players in the team - a World Cup winner and the PFA Player of the Year - coming out and hammering the owners, hammering the sporting director and criticising the manager, all in the space of a week means the players have completely gone.

"But there a number of these players who have been a wrecking ball through managers for the last three or four years and it looks like, unfortunately, it's happening again.

Talking about Michael Carrick's emotional address at the start of his press conference on Friday, Neville said: "When you're starting to have to justify the values of this football club, citing [Wayne] Rooney, [Sir Matt] Busby, [Sir Alex] Ferguson, that message can only be to the players. There's millions around the world who don't need reminding of what Manchester United is.

"If you're having to remind them of history, values and personality traits to play for this club, you're at a pretty low point."

Asked about Fernandes' quotes about Carrick's tactics, Neville added: "They're devastating. It's a direct attack on the manager.

"If you go back 25 years, these players would never be anywhere near the club, never mind the pitch. They'd be gone. Finished.

"But Manchester United aren't in that position anymore and neither is Michael Carrick.

"It was a horrible press conference to watch. It was very emotional.

"There has to be a consequence, for Michael's own reputation. He's got to do it for himself.

"Fernandes has been a fantastic player for this club, he's been world-class at times. But let's be really blunt about it - he's played awfully this season. His standards have been really poor.

articles.title: Courtois no viaja a Barcelona y es baja definitiva
articles.standfirst: El belga quería apurar sus opciones pese a que el Madrid anunció su baja por gripe... pero finalmente se queda en tierra
articles.summary: El belga quería apurar sus opciones pese a que el Madrid anunció su baja por gripe... pero finalmente se queda en tierra
articles.body: El Clásico está perdido para Thibaut Courtois. El Real Madrid anunció este domingo por la mañana que el portero se caía de la convocatoria por un proceso gripal, pero el belga quería seguir intentándolo hasta el final para estar en el partido contra el Barcelona. Sin embargo, en la última hora se ha conocido que finalmente el portero se queda en tierra por este proceso y será baja definitiva ante el máximo rival en el Camp Nou. "Vamos a ver cómo avanzan las horas y se va encontrando mejor. Si es así, volará hacia Barcelona", explicaban desde Valdebebas. "A ver si puede recuperarse al 100% y vuela", añadían. El parte médico del club apuntaba a su ausencia, pero la posibilidad de que viaje sigue abierta si mejora durante las próximas horas. Courtois no quería tirar la toalla y estaba dispuesto a apurar los plazos para intentar llegar a una cita importante, aunque finalmente será Lunin el que ocupe su plaza. La mañana, caótica y desconcertante a partes iguales, lanzó el primer golpe al Real Madrid de Mourinho. "Tiene un gripazo", apuntaban desde Valdebebas, antes de que un segundo diagnóstico, mucho más gráfico, terminara de dibujar el escenario: "Está reventado". Un virus había agarrado con fuerza al portero belga y le había dejado KO, hasta el punto de que el club anunciaba su baja para el Clásico. Pero Thibaut, que no ha dicho su última palabra, quiere seguir intentándolo. El desconcierto de la mañana contrasta con la cautela que ahora impera en el club. El parte médico apuntaba a una ausencia segura, pero la posibilidad de que Courtois viaje sigue abierta si experimenta una mejoría suficiente. El belga quiere agotar todos los plazos antes de asumir que no podrá estar ante el Barcelona. En cualquier caso, el Madrid también tiene claro que cuenta con garantías bajo palos si su portero titular no llega a tiempo. "Tenemos a Lunin. Que es muy bueno", aseguran desde el club, conscientes de que el ucraniano está preparado para asumir la responsabilidad y para rebajar la preocupación.

articles.title: Un Clásico de anuncio: "Lamine es naturalidad, frescura y chulería"; "Mbappé ha construido un estatus de exclusividad"; "Son dos empresas"
articles.standfirst: El azulgrana y el blanco son imanes para las marcas, seducidas por dos perfiles diferentes con un impacto analizado por expertos en el sector
articles.summary: El azulgrana y el blanco son imanes para las marcas, seducidas por dos perfiles diferentes con un impacto analizado por expertos en el sector
articles.body: Es posible establecer una rutina sin salir del universo publicitario que cobija a Lamine Yamal (Esplugues de Llobregat, 2007) y Kylian Mbappé (París, 1998). Se puede dormir en un hotel que publicite el madridista, desayunar con la bebida que anuncia el azulgrana, ponerse las gafas que muestra el galo, salir a la calle con los auriculares que son sello del culé y el francés y por supuesto, dar asistencias y meter goles con las marcas deportivas de cada uno. Es la otra cara del Clásico, el mejor escaparate del mundo. Cada movimiento comercial de estos emperadores icónicos provoca espasmos en las cuentas de negocio de las empresas. Lamine Yamal (59'8 millones de seguidores en Instagram), con vínculos con Adidas, Visa, Powerade, Beats, Nesquik, Mc Donald's, Oppo o American Eagle, y Kylian Mbappé (136 millones), ligado entre otros a On, Hublot, Oakley, Christian Dior, All Accor o Loewe, son imanes para las marcas. Ambos, campeones del mundo a los 19 años, no encuentran barreras en su expansión comercial. Los expertos en marketing y publicidad analizan el impacto de estas dos estrellas, sus puntos fuertes y débiles y la conexión con las grandes audiencias. Lo que pase en el Camp Nou no se queda en el Camp Nou. Aitana Pascual, creative strategist de la Agencia Creativa Jungle PS21, estima que el punto fuerte de Lamine Yamal "es la conexión con los zetas: su naturalidad, frescura y chulería marcan la identidad de cada una de sus campañas. El débil creo que es la sobreexposición y presencia en multitud de campañas de cualquier categoría, quedando en segundo plano el sentido de la unión. Al final, es un chaval de 19 años que acepta propuestas porque molan sin una madurez mediática capaz de filtrar cada proyecto con un ojo más crítico y pulido". Para Aitana Pascual, "Mbappé sí hace un buen cribado. No por la cantidad, sino por el tipo de marca. Ha sabido construir su estatus de icono global con una personalidad más selectiva y exclusiva. El lado débil viene de la mano de esto último. Al ser tan exigente y cuidadoso con lo que comunica puede parecer algo prepotente y distante para la gente". El enganche de Lamine Yamal con la juventud lo expresó con claridad Nesquik al fichar al azulgrana. "En Nesquik queremos seguir inspirando a las generaciones de adolescentes y jóvenes a adoptar una actitud positiva ante los retos". Alfonso Fontalba, fundador de Liten Lemon, agencia de marketing digital, apunta que Lamine y Mbappé "cuentan con una proyección internacional, los conoce todo el mundo y además pertenecen a dos clubes conocidísimos. Lamine es muy joven, le caracteriza el barrio, ser familia de inmigrantes, un contexto urbano que le ayuda. Está en un momento de crecimiento brutal. Lo malo para él puede ser que a veces, por ese contexto, se mete en algunos charcos. El punto débil de Mbappé es que a veces, con todo su derecho, expresa posiciones políticas que no le benefician". Mbappé dio recientemente un volantazo. Dejó a Nike, la marca que le acompañaba desde niño, y entró en la escuadra de On, una firma suiza que va mordiendo décimas al mercado. El futbolista mostró su satisfacción por "construir algo enteramente nuevo juntos que dé forma al juego del mañana”. La empresa, con participación de Roger Federer, y con Thierry Henry de director deportivo, se disparó más de un 7 por ciento en Wall Street. Las campañas con ambos concitan una expectación universal. Pascual apunta que con Lamine "sería más arriesgada en 'el cómo'. Buscaría formas de conectar con la gente fuera de los convencionalismos publicitarios. Como lo que hizo TwoJeys durante un Clásico. La marca de joyas 'patrocinó' los brackets de Lamine y consiguió que al celebrar su gol los enseñara con un gesto provocador". Con Mbappé incide en que buscaría "una conexión más cómplice con sus valores y personalidad y así aprovechar esa percepción de exclusivo y distante para construir aspiracionalidad. Creo que lo que hace con Oakley y Rimowa tiene mucho de esto: elegancia, coherencia en su discurso y cierto estatus". Fontalba remarca cómo "cualquier marca desea un altavoz como el de estos dos futbolistas. Lamine es de marcas más urbanas para un público más joven, tipo tik tok; Mbappé es más de marcas de lujo, una franja de edad más avanzada". La asociación de Mbappé con la exclusividad es patente. El francés se integra en el engranaje del imperio Louis Vuitton. A través de esa firma participa en Rimowa (equipaje y maletas), Christian Dior (ropa y belleza) y Hublot (relojes). En una reciente concentración con Francia, Mbappé lucía una sudadera de Dior con un valor de 3.800 euros. Real Madrid y Barcelona son planetarios. Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé también, tanto que son capaces de volar sin el motor de los clubes. Pascual añade que "el respaldo de un club grande aporta credibilidad siendo un comodín para las marcas, pero aún así funcionan muy bien de manera autónoma". Fontalba coincide en que ambas estrellas "no necesitan un club porque ya son una marca, pero el club les da más potencia. El caso de Lamine es más especial. Sólo ha estado en un club, el Barcelona. Es como si el logo alrededor de Lamine fuera su barrio, el código postal de Barcelona. En el Mundial no se podía cruzar una calle en Nueva York sin ver una imagen de Lamine con la camiseta de España o el Barça. Lamine y Mbappé son empresas, megatransatlánticos". Pascual destaca que las marcas "ya no compran tanto a un futbolista por el escudo que vista, sino por el universo cultural propio que lleva consigo. Club y futbolista ahora están más separados que nunca. Bellerín, Borja Iglesias o Alexia son ejemplos de esto. Un chaval puede ser de Osasuna, del Rayo o del Athletic y conectar con Lamine por expresar su apoyo al pueblo palestino y consigue cierta simpatía hacia las marcas con las que trabaja". ¿Qué se busca al enlazar una marca con uno de estos referentes? Hay presente y futuro. Por eso, Pascual piensa que en Lamine "hasta ahora se ha buscado un vínculo temprano y duradero para adueñarse de su curva de crecimiento. Ahora, en un momento en el que Lamine está tan saturado, puede que la cosa cambie y busquen una historia más grande que contar que beneficie tanto a las marcas como a él mismo". Las últimas estimaciones de Forbes señalan que Lamine Yamal factura 20 millones de euros anuales por conceptos publicitarios. Mbappé se va hasta los 30. Y no parece haber límites para estas dos vetas doradas. La experta señala que con Mbappé "buscan seguridad sin renunciar al alcance y a la repercusión mediática de un futbolista como él: un atleta con el criterio para vetar cualquier comunicación que venga de comida rápida, juego online o alcohol no representa un riesgo para la imagen de las marcas, sino un sello de certeza y estabilidad". Las vías de comunicación para estos dos gigantes son infinitas. Fontalba manifiesta que los dos futbolistas "son efectivos en cualquier sistema de comunicación. El fútbol se sigue de los 5 a los 90 años. Si Lamine hace algo para la Kings League es normal que se vehicule más el mensaje en redes sociales. Si Mbappé hace algo de Louis Vuitton, para un público de más edad, se basa más la campaña en cartelería". Aitana Pascual estima que en Lamine "destacaría su impacto indiscutible en el ecosistema digital. Su fuerza no radica en una gran producción, sino en aquello que domina de forma orgánica con códigos puros de su generación: se suma a 'trends', sube vídeos con su novia, utiliza cuentas secundarias para 'stalkear', prescinde de foto de perfil. Encorsetarlo en un formato muy tradicional diluiría su frescura". Sobre Mbappé, incide en que su medio "podría ser cualquier formato siempre y cuando se juegue con su discreción, misterio e iconicidad. Por ejemplo, cuando Mbappé habla, sube el pan. Así, cualquier pieza donde el peso recaiga en sus declaraciones podría trascender". En la publicidad tampoco hay victorias seguras. Pascual recuerda que "la presencia de una celebridad puede comprar atención, pero no garantiza eficacia publicitaria. El reto es que esa atención se traduzca en recuerdo y diferenciación para ambas marcas interesadas (marca comercial y futbolista). El Clásico del anuncio está preparado.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza: "El hambre de competir es lo que define a este equipo"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Sevilla adelantó que Stassin, Guridi y Kochorashvili están disponibles
articles.summary: El entrenador del Sevilla adelantó que Stassin, Guridi y Kochorashvili están disponibles
articles.body: Luis García Plaza compareció este domingo con motivo de la décima jornada de LaLiga EA Sports, en la que el Sevilla recibirá a Osasuna en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. "Muchas ganas de disfrutar del Sánchez-Pizjuán y tener comunión con los nuestros. Cada partido es muy difícil, cuesta un mundo y cada victoria es oro molido. El equipo está con muchas ganas de volver a ganar, pero sobre todo de pelear y competir", arrancó el técnico nervionense. Banda derecha. "Puede ser que probemos con Rubén, Chidera, Alfon o Félix, todos son diestros y el que juegue ojalá lo haga bien, ahora vienen cuatro partidos en doce días, entrenamientos muy pocos y todos están preparados para aportar. Tienen que aportar todos". Duelos con Arrasate. "Tengo muy buena relación con él. Las estadísticas no me importan mucho, lo importante es que ganemos. Jagoba creo que encaja al dedillo en Pamplona, en Osasuna, con su filosofía, ya el otro día se vio un equipo muy de su estilo, muy intenso, con mucho duelo y balón directo, apretando muy fuerte… para mí es uno de los equipos más físicos de la categoría en cuanto a altura y fuerza. Ojalá le pueda ganar porque sumar 17 a esas alturas sería una cifra de puntos muy buena". Recuperar el foco. "Sigue en dinámica buena. A veces hay partidos incontrolables, pero el equipo está bien y tiene que seguir compitiendo como ahora. LaLiga es una carrera de fondo, nos centramos en Osasuna. El hambre de competir que tenemos es lo que define al equipo". Vuelta de Stassin, Guridi y Kochorashvili. "Están todos disponibles, algunos no están para jugar 90 minutos ni 45, voy a tener que dejar a uno fuera, pero están todos bien. No digo quién, no hay que ser muy listos para saber quién va a estar más o menos tiempo. Son cuatro partidos a los que llegamos con toda la plantilla aunque algunos no estén para 90 minutos". Explicaciones del CTA. "Cuando acabó el partido pasé página, siempre estaré en la línea de actuación del club, pero estoy ya centrado en Osasuna desde que terminamos en el Bernabéu". Renovación Castrín. "Me gustaría, claro. Conmigo se ha consolidado en Primera División y en el Sevilla, pero es pregunta para el director deportivo, Castrín y el presidente. No sé cómo van las negociaciones". Opciones en el centro del campo. "Creo que las plantillas están para que pases momentos de dificultad con bajas, es importante que todos estén, Manu Bueno lo poco que ha jugado ha sido de lo mejor del equipo y se está ganando el sitio a base de trabajo y de que cada vez que aparece está bien. Eso es la plantilla del Sevilla, su aportación ha sido decisiva. Estoy contento con todos".

articles.title: England win Cerebral Palsy World Cup for first time
articles.summary: Sam Dewhirst and David Porcher score the goals as England beat the United States in the final of the Cerebral Palsy World Cup in Atlanta.
articles.body:
England have won the Cerebral Palsy World Cup for the first time by beating the United States 2-1 in a thrilling final.

The hosts took the lead in Atlanta from a corner with three minutes left but Sam Dewhirst equalised to take the tie to extra time.

And the Para Lions won it when David Porcher fired home after Dewhirst's shot was saved.

England cerebral palsy head coach Jack Rutter said the win was historic for the sport.

"The amount of sacrifice these players and staff have put in to achieve this goal is incredible.

"We were coming here with hope of maybe winning a medal and I can't believe we actually won the World Cup for the first time.

"I'm very, very proud of all the staff and all the players."

The win comes after England's powerchair squad were beaten by France in their World Cup final on Friday. , external

articles.title: After win over Ole Miss, Texas QB Arch Manning says that he 'kind of likes being disregarded'
articles.summary: Manning rushed for two scores and threw for another in Texas' 34-27 victory.
articles.body:
Arch Manning found himself in a bit of an unfamiliar role heading into No. 19 Texas' win over No. 7 Ole Miss.

The Longhorns QB had struggled with untimely turnovers in Texas' losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Not long after the Florida game, ESPN reported that his backup, redshirt freshman KJ Lacey, would receive an increase in first-team reps.

After throwing two interceptions in the fourth quarter of the Oklahoma loss, Manning fumbled on Texas' final drive against Florida. The Longhorns were near midfield with less than two minutes to go and needed a field goal for the tie or a touchdown to take the lead.

That loss led to a visit to his parents' house the next day.

"It was a hard Sunday, I went over to their place and damn near bawled, cried to them," Manning said.

It seemed farfetched that coach Steve Sarkisian would actually bench Manning. During the week, he noted that Manning was "edgy" and that he appreciated the shift in demeanor following the Longhorns' losses.

Save for having to exit for a mandatory medical check for one play in the second half, Manning played the entire game as Texas hung on in the second half for a 34-27 win over the Rebels , despite blowing a 21-point halftime lead.

Manning scored the go-ahead touchdown and said after the game that he had embraced being in a different position.

"I've been hyped up all my life, preseason and all that stuff," Manning said after the game . "I think I kind of like being disregarded."

The victory over Ole Miss was a massive confidence boost for both team and quarterback. A loss to the Rebels would have put Texas on the brink of missing the College Football Playoff for the second time in Manning's two seasons as a starter.

But it's also not a sign that Texas is suddenly a national title contender again, either.

Manning turned the ball over three times. He threw two interceptions, including an incredibly ill-advised throw in the fourth quarter. He also fumbled on Texas' first possession of the second half thanks to pressure from the side of the offensive line that Trevor Goosby typically occupies. The star left tackle went down with a leg injury in the first half and had to be carted off the field.

Wide receiver Cam Coleman also suffered a shoulder injury in the second half. Sarkisian didn't have details about either player's injury, but noted that neither "looked very good."

Texas was already playing without star edge rusher Colin Simmons and running back Hollywood Smothers. The pass rush didn't sack Trinidad Chambliss, but it consistently got enough pressure through the middle to deflect passes. Chambliss completed fewer than 50% of his passing attempts for the first time in his Ole Miss career.

And now both the Rebels and Longhorns are tied in the middle of a messy SEC. As Georgia and Kentucky are the only teams in the conference with one league loss, eight teams — including Texas and Ole Miss — are tied with two losses and another four have three.

articles.title: Man Utd captain Bruno Fernandes left on bench by manager Michael Carrick during Bournemouth defeat
articles.summary: Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes is left on the bench for Sunday's 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, following his criticism of manager Michael Carrick.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and left on the bench for Sunday's 3-0 Premier League defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Fernandes' place in the team had been debated since his explosive comments after Wednesday's Champions League humiliation by Como, when he blamed manager Michael Carrick for United's tactics in the 4-1 defeat and his failure to alter them.

Carrick refused to say in his media conference on Friday whether Fernandes would be dropped.

That happened, with the Portugal midfielder left on the bench as United's winless run in all competitions extended to eight matches.

Asked on Sky Sports before the match about the selection, Carrick called Fernandes' omission "a football decision".

He added: "When you have options it's always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want."

Harry Maguire took over as captain, with Mason Mount handed a playmaking role along with Youri Tielemans.

It was only the sixth time Fernandes had been left on the bench for a Premier League game. The previous two, at the end of the 2024-25 season, were to keep him fresh for important Europa League games.

They had won just one of their previous 10 Premier League games without Fernandes in the starting XI (drawn three, lost six), beating Newcastle 1-0 in December.

Bournemouth beat Man Utd to increase pressure on Carrick

Fernandes left out - Man Utd hammered, Bournemouth brilliant - how they rated

Matheus Cunha was also on the bench after being replaced at half-time in Italy, along with Lisandro Martinez, who spoke out about the United hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid this month.

Martinez started at Leeds last week but was left out of the Como game because of injury.

Carrick said before the Bournemouth match that it was "touch and go" for the Argentina defender to start "but it wasn't worth the risk".

Cunha was brought on at half-time against the Cherries, while Martinez came off the bench during the second half.

Carrick referred to the Como debacle in his programme notes for Sunday's game.

" Manchester United is a truly great football club," he said.

"Our standards and values have been set out over generations and are very important to me.

"As a group, we have a duty to represent you in a manner that is befitting of those principles.

"Wednesday's performance was extremely disappointing in many ways. Today we have to show what we are all about.

"We all need to stick together but we know that we absolutely have to do better for you. Now, as a group, we need to put in a performance that your support deserves."

'It's half a sanction again' - what the pundits said

Former Crystal Palace striker Clinton Morrison on BBC Radio 5 Live: " Manchester United are nowhere near good enough.

"I've praised Carrick a lot but I'm not praising him now - he had to bring Bruno Fernandes on at half-time. I don't care what the situation is, you're 2-0 down.

"I understand Cunha coming on but I would have put Bruno on as well.

"If you want to make a statement about not having Bruno Fernandes because of the comments he made, just leave him out of the squad. Having him on the bench opens him up to criticism.

"Just be honest, don't say it was tactical, you did it because of the comments he made."

European football expert Julien Laurens on BBC Radio 5 Live before kick-off: "I think if the sanctions against Lisandro Martinez had been the right ones, I'm not sure Bruno would have said that after the Como game.

"It's about boundaries and having to set limits for your own squad so things like that don't happen and now, for two senior players within the space of six days to go after the sporting director, your owners, your manager, your staff is just embarrassing. It's such a circus.

"Leave him at home, he doesn't need to be on the bench - it's half of a sanction again. He's just going to be behind Carrick and I don't think he should be there full stop."

Ex- Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher on Sky Sports before kick-off : "Bruno Fernandes is Manchester United 's best player, we can't get away from that. PFA Player of the Year last year. He had to make the stand, Michael Carrick.

"Even though he's the best player, there will be a lot of people who don't actually like playing with him in the United team. He's permanently throwing his arms up at people, he's basically saying, 'you're not good enough to play with me'."

That's what we see from Fernandes a lot when things aren't going right for United.

Daryl : Fernandes, and anyone else not fully behind the manager and his way of thinking, should be dropped. End of.

Tom : Very brave of Carrick but also the right decision. Bruno has been poor this season, only one good game against Ipswich . He spends too much time dragging the team down with his silly childish antics. He was the captain, talk about not leading by example.

Sam : We're all aware of Bruno's quality but his form has largely been pretty dire so far this season. His outburst may have been better received if he was still performing like last season, but ultimately he isn't. Harsh to drop him perhaps but absolutely understandable. I would've done the same.

Josh : Fair play to Carrick for dropping Bruno. It's one thing if Fernandes had gone to Carrick in private and said what he said. It's another thing to do it publicly in front of cameras.
