articles.title: Los gestos que delatan a Mourinho y Flick: "Dijo 'no, nunca o nada' el doble de lo habitual..."
articles.standfirst: Esteban Pascual, especialista en análisis del comportamiento y la lectura de tells, analiza para MARCA los gestos, silencios y respuestas de ambos técnicos
articles.summary: Esteban Pascual, especialista en análisis del comportamiento y la lectura de tells, analiza para MARCA los gestos, silencios y respuestas de ambos técnicos
articles.body: Antes del Clásico, cada palabra cuenta. Y también lo que Mourinho y Flick prefieren callarse. En sus ruedas de prensa, los dos entrenadores dejaron gestos, silencios y respuestas que no pasaron inadvertidos para Esteban Pascual, especialista en análisis del comportamiento y la lectura de tells, que analiza para MARCA cómo se comportaron ante las preguntas más comprometidas de la previa del partido en el Camp Nou. El momento más significativo de las dos ruedas de prensa llegó con la polémica arbitral. Martínez Munuera había sido confirmado para dirigir el encuentro después de que su nombre se filtrara antes de que el club recibiera la comunicación oficial. Mourinho se quejó de esa situación, pero es su reacción la que centra la atención de Esteban. El portugués elevó las cejas y los hombros al mismo tiempo mientras expresa su malestar. Para Esteban, Mourinho se estaba guardando su opinión sobre los árbitros para después del partido. El entrenador pone el foco en la filtración, pero no expone todo lo que piensa sobre la cuestión arbitral. Flick tampoco quiso entrar en un terreno que pueda volverse en su contra. El alemán suspira, mide sus palabras y verbaliza su preocupación por las consecuencias de sus declaraciones: “No quiero ningún titular”. Si Mourinho expresa su queja sin revelar toda su posición, Flick opta por contener el mensaje desde el principio. "Llegó muy preparado y se mantuvo impasible, salvo un trago de saliva al hablar de títulos", explica. La lectura de Esteban, jugador de póker con ranking mundial y embajador de PokerStars, no se limita a los árbitros. Cuando le preguntan por su regreso al Camp Nou, Mourinho afirmó que es “igual que ir a otro estadio”. Sin embargo, el analista interpreta que el portugués intenta restar trascendencia a una visita que sabe que no es una más. Responde rápido y pasa a la siguiente pregunta, sin detenerse en lo que supone volver a un escenario de semejante dimensión. Flick, en cambio, transmite confianza cuando asegura que su equipo está preparado. Esteban observa que asiente durante toda la frase y entiende ese movimiento como una señal de que cree realmente en sus jugadores. Dos respuestas distintas ante la presión: Mourinho intenta cerrar el asunto y Flick refuerza públicamente la confianza en su equipo. Las palabras respaldan parte de las diferencias que Esteban aprecia en ambos entrenadores. En comparación con sus ruedas de prensa anteriores, Mourinho pronuncia “no”, “nunca” o “nada” el doble de veces de lo habitual, mientras que sus respuestas duran menos de la mitad. Flick, por su parte, se mantiene dentro de sus registros habituales. El portugués apenas pierde la compostura durante su intervención. Uno de los pocos detalles que destaca Esteban aparece cuando se habla de títulos: Mourinho traga saliva. La lectura global sitúa al técnico madridista como el que mejor mantiene su cara de póker, gracias a una actitud preparada e impasible que apenas deja espacio para interpretar sus reacciones. Esteban aplica al fútbol los principios que ha aprendido en las mesas de póker. Allí, los tells son señales que pueden ofrecer pistas sobre la mano de un jugador. En una rueda de prensa, pueden aparecer en una mirada que se desvía, una respuesta que se acorta o un gesto que acompaña una pregunta incómoda. Pero ningún gesto demuestra por sí solo que alguien miente. La clave está en comparar cada reacción con el comportamiento habitual de la persona, encontrar varias señales coincidentes y analizar el contexto en el que aparecen.

articles.title: Arch Manning Reacts to 'Edgy' Quote from Sarkisian After Texas' Win vs. Ole Miss amid Benching Buzz
articles.summary: There was no shortage of noise surrounding Arch Manning after Steve Sarkisian told reporters ahead of Saturday's game against Ole Miss his QB1 status would be evaluated, but the Texas head coach liked what he saw from the "edgy" signal-caller in the 34-27 win.
articles.body:
There was no shortage of noise surrounding Arch Manning after Steve Sarkisian told reporters ahead of Saturday's game against Ole Miss his QB1 status would be evaluated, but the Texas head coach liked what he saw from the "edgy" signal-caller in the 34-27 win.

"I was edgy? I don't know what that means," Manning said after the win, per Schuyler Dixon of the Associated Press. "But yeah, I think I had a chip on my shoulder all week. I've got to continue to play like that."

His comments come after Sarkisian told reporters Thursday that Manning was "edgy" all week leading up to the contest.

After the game, the coach said , "One thing I know about Arch Manning, he's a fighter. I like the edgy, kind of borderline arrogant, full-of-swagger Arch. I just feel like that's when he's at his best."

Some anxiety or at least uneasiness surrounding the Texas program heading into the game was to be expected.

It wasn't just that Manning's status as the team's starter was being discussed. The Longhorns also lost two straight games to rival Oklahoma and Florida, putting their College Football Playoff hopes in serious jeopardy.

A third straight conference loss would have put them in a position where they would have needed to win out just to have an outside chance at making the 12-team field even with quality wins over Ohio State and Tennessee on their resume.

Manning immediately responded to the pressure, though, and led Texas to a 24-3 halftime advantage with a touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo and a touchdown run of his own. His early performance would have been even better if Cam Coleman didn't drop what should have been a touchdown on a deep ball.

The visitors recovered a Manning fumble for a touchdown before Trinidad Chambliss directed two touchdown drives to tie the game at 24 in the fourth quarter. The Texas crowd was stunned, and it felt like the season was slipping away with the team's highly regarded quarterback throwing two interceptions in addition to the lost fumble.

That's when Manning directed a six-play, 80-yard drive that he capped off with a touchdown run to take the lead for good. Ole Miss had a chance to tie it on the final play, but Chambliss' heave was intercepted in the end zone.

"When he shows that fire in his belly that he had tonight, I think the team responds to that," Sarkisian said of Manning. "I'm just very proud of him because this isn't easy. His world, his life is different than anybody else I've ever been around that's been part of this sport. But the guy keeps coming back, and so we're lucky to have him as our guy."

The CFP is still well within sight for the Longhorns after their third quality win of the season, and now Manning has some momentum after responding to a difficult situation within Saturday's game after what was likely a challenging week of speculation about his starting status.

articles.title: El Inter tumba el muro de De Gea y neutraliza el gol de Álex Jiménez
articles.standfirst: Remontada frente a la Fiorentina en el descuento para evitar que la Lazio amarre el liderato de la Serie A en solitario
articles.summary: Remontada frente a la Fiorentina en el descuento para evitar que la Lazio amarre el liderato de la Serie A en solitario
articles.body: La Fiorentina ya se veía sacando los tres puntos del Meazza gracias al 'bombazo' de Álex Jiménez en su retorno a Milán y el muro levantado por De Gea. En el tiempo de descuento, sin embargo, el Inter logró darle la vuelta al encuentro para conservar su invicto en Serie A y no permitir a la Lazio amarrar el liderato en solitario. Sin Lautaro, ausente por lesión por tercer partido consecutivo, fue Pio Esposito quien acompañó a Marcus Thuram en la doble punta del Inter. Chivu, además, dio descanso a Dimarco y ubicó a Mkhitaryan junto a Calhanoglu y Barella en la medular. La mayor novedad fue el debut de Provedel bajo palos. Mastantuono, como suele ser habitual, partió como extremo derecho en una Fiorentina donde arrancaron desde el inicio De Gea, Álex Jiménez y Valdepeñas. El propio Mastantuono registró la primera ocasión del encuentro con una falta desde el 'piquito' derecho del área que estrelló contra la barrera. Fue, eso sí, el único acercamiento de una Fiorentina que priorizó juntarse atrás y cederle la iniciativa a un Inter al que le costó comenzar a imprimirle ritmo al encuentro. Fue Barella, con un disparo manso centrado desde el balcón del área, quien protagonizó la primera de los 'neroazzurri'. A partir de entonces, eso sí, subió el nivel de agresividad y empezó a ahogar a una Fiorentina incapaz de desplegarse. Tuvo que aparecer el mejor De Gea, con dos intervenciones ante Marcus Thuram y otro sobre Pio Esposito, para mantener las tablas al descanso. Resarciéndose de su última actuación ante el Como. No quería el Inter que se difuminase el impulso con el que había cerrado la primera parte... mientras que Vanoli tuvo que reemplazar a Pongracic por Viery por lesión nada más volver del vestuario. Continuó el 'goteo' de ocasiones y, pasada la hora de partido, Chivu refrescó la punta de ataque con la entrada de Bonny por un Pio Esposito que apenas había tenido peso en el encuentro. Sólo un minutos después, sin embargo, Álex Jiménez enmudeció al Meazza... a pesar de estar mermado. Recibió en zona de tres cuartos, levantó la cabeza y, consciente de que nadie le 'flotaba', conectó un 'misil' que se coló por la escuadra del palo corto de Provedel. Quinto gol que genera el canterano del Real Madrid desde su desembarco en la Fiorentina. El Inter, a partir de entonces, se volcó al ataque. Se reclamó un penalti de Viery sobre Marcus Thuram, mientras que Carlos Augusto mandó al travesaño dos servicios de Calhanoglu a balón parado. Vanoli rearmó su sector derecho reemplazando a Álex Jiménez y Mastantuono... mientras que Chivu dio entrada a Dimarco, Zielinski y Sucic de una tacada para, a cinco minutos para el final, tirar del canterano Lavelli a la desesperada. Resistía la Fiorentina, que cerró el partido con línea de cinco, como buenamente podía. Nada más entrar en el tiempo de descuento, sin embargo, Marcus Thuram se inventó una genialidad para batir a De Gea desde la frontal y, con el tiempo ya cumplido, fue víctima de un penalti infantil por parte de Valdepeñas convertido de manera inapelable por Zielinski. Sigue sin convencer el Inter... pero llegará con la moral reforzada al 'Derby della Madonnina'.

articles.title: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic: Camilo Duran's 10th goal of season restores four-point lead at top as Hibs remain bottom of Scottish Premiership
articles.summary: Report as Celtic beat Hibernian at Easter Road; Owen Elding fired Hibs to an early lead that was cancelled out by Jason Kerr's own-goal; Camilo Duran fired the Hoops ahead before half-time; Celtic restored their four-point lead at the top of the Premiership; Hibs remain bottom
articles.body:
Martin O'Neill was looking for a response after Celtic's midweek Europa League misery, but Owen Elding fired the struggling Hibees ahead just three minutes into the game.

The hosts, winless under new manager Marink Reedijk, then handed the Hoops the equaliser two minutes later when Jason Kerr headed into his own net from a corner.

Kasper Hogh returned to Celtic's starting line-up, but the record signing's lack of confidence was evident when he wasted two chances to put the champions ahead.

Camilo Duran scored his 10th goal to put Celtic ahead at the break, hammering the ball into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Mika Baur tested Raphael Sallinger from distance, and survived a late flurry of pressure from Hibs who even brought defender Grant Hanley on to play up front.

Hibs remain a point adrift at the foot of the table, without a league win since August, while O'Neill's Celtic have won nine of their last 10 in the Premiership.

There were a couple of blemishes for Celtic.

Substitute Alistair Johnston's return from injury lasted less than 20 minutes before he had to go off, while £11m forward Hogh - restored to the starting line-up after notching in just one of his 13 previous matches - again drew a blank before being replaced in the 64th minute.

3: GOAL HIBS! Joe Newell takes a quick free-kick, Celtic switch off and Owen Elding fires into the far corner.

5: SAVE! Raphael Sallinger gets his fingertips to Callum McGregor's shot to turn it wide.

5: GOAL CELTIC! Jason Kerr heads into his own net from a corner with no Celtic players near him.

12: CHANCE! Osmand with a brilliant cross into the box, but Hogh can't get on the end of it.

14: SAVE! Hogh does get on the end of a ball from Osmand this time, only for Sallinger to produce a brilliant save.

40: CHANCE! Thibault Klidje beats Colby Donovan, but gets too much on his cross and the ball flies past the far post.

43: CLOSE! Donovan totally misjudges a long ball and Klidje gets on the end of it. One-on-one with the keeper, he sends his shot over the bar.

43: GOAL CELTIC! Camilo Duran inside and fires into the far corner. Hibs left to pay for that chance seconds ago.

47: SAVE! Mika Baur hammers a shot from outside the box, but Sallinger does well to keep it out.

67: WIDE! Haissem Hassan wants to make an impact after coming on but fires wide from just outside the area.

72: BLOCK! Duran takes aim from the edge of the box, but Kerr blocks.

83: SAVE! Grant Hanley almost equalises! Rabbi Matondo's deflected shot is just out of reach and Sam Johnstone gathers.

86: BLOCK! Crucial from Carter-Vickers as Hibs look to snatch a point.

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd thinks Celtic have to stop looking at Kasper Hogh's £11m price tag, and stick with Camilo Duran through the middle.

"If Celtic hadn't paid £11m for Kasper Hogh, would they be persevering with him at the top end of the pitch because he's offering absolutely nothing," he said.

"You look at Camilo Duran, any time he goes through the middle Celtic look a far better team. I can understand why he's frustrated.

"He's got another match winner today, but I can totally understand his stance because if I am the man who's firing the goals he has been Celtic's best striker.

"Why is he getting forced out of the way just to accommodate someone because of the price? Kasper Hogh has offered absolutely nothing for me."

On Hibs' dismal winless run of seven league games, Boyd added: "I think the fans have had enough,"

"They're asking questions of the hierarchy all the way down.

"Reedijk has come in, he has tried to put a positive spin but I'm afraid to say I don't really see what direction Hibs are going in.

"To throw him [Grant Hanley] on up front sums up where Hibs are at right now. They are miles off it."

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill speaking to Sky Sports:

"Given the circumstances, given the conditions, given the fact that we didn't play all that well, I thought it was our best win of the season.

"Difficult to come here in normal circumstances and to come from a goal behind after a couple of minutes as well too, I'm really delighted.

"Perseverance of the side, as much as anything else, didn't play really well at all in the game. But it doesn't matter, we've won the game and that shows a bit of character."

On Kasper Hogh's goalless run continuing, he added: "I keep saying this, the goals will come. I'm not just saying this to please myself or anything. I think they will come,"

"If you're a box player, sometimes it might not matter about what happens further out the field at the end of it all. But it'll come good for him."

Asked about Alistair Johnston's short return, O'Neill said: "Alistair's felt something again, a little bit high up in his hamstring. We're a wee bit concerned about it,"

"We'll have to see. That would be a blow if he's out.

"Naturally, I think when you're coming back from these particular injuries, you do have a concern about it. We'll see how he is."

Hibernian manager Marink Reedijk on Sky Sports:

"Overall we were the equals of Celtic. I think that's a compliment towards the team.

"We kept on fighting, I think we kept on in the match and we got the opportunities to at least get a draw here and I think we deserved that.

"I believe that what we need to do is to take the positives out of this. I saw a team which was intense, wanted to fight, created chances and I think that Celtic didn't create until the end when we started to play a little bit more opportunistic.

"That's a big compliment for us because they have quality up front but they weren't able to unlock that."

articles.title: Crystal Palace 1-3 Chelsea Women: Melvine Malard double sees Sonia Bompastor's side come from behind to win
articles.summary: Match report and free match highlights as Chelsea beat Crystal Palace 3-1 in the Women's Super League; Molly Bartrip put Crystal Palace ahead but goals from Melvine Malard and Sandy Baltimore secured the win for Sonia Bompastor's side
articles.body:
The Blues dominated from the opening stages, having two efforts cleared off the line and forcing Pauline Payraud-Magnin into a smart double save inside the first 15 minutes. They were punished for not taking their chances, as Molly Bartrip bundled home from a corner to score Palace's first goal against Chelsea in eight games between the two teams.

Erin Cuthbert and Baltimore were introduced at the break and from then on Chelsea were in control. They equalised in stunning fashion as Melvine Malard, moments after missing an opening goal, unleashed a strike from 25 yards that left Payraud-Magnin stranded.

Malard completed the comeback, heading home after a brilliant Baltimore run that saw her beat three Palace defenders before delivering. Baltimore then got her name on the scoresheet with a late penalty to seal the points.

The win means Chelsea temporarily go top of the WSL table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Manchester United.

articles.title: Henrik Pedersen: Sheffield Wednesday sack head coach after less than 15 months in charge
articles.summary: Sheffield Wednesday sack head coach Henrik Pedersen after less than 15 months in charge following consecutive defeats.
articles.body:
Sheffield Wednesday have sacked head coach Henrik Pedersen after less than 15 months in charge following two League One defeats in five days.

Pedersen's final match was a 2-0 defeat at Doncaster Rovers in a South Yorkshire derby on Saturday, when fans called for the 48-year-old to leave after seeing their side concede twice inside the first 17 minutes.

Matt Hamshaw, who was sacked by Rotherham United after less than a year in charge last season before becoming a coach at Wednesday in August, has taken over on an interim basis and will oversee the visit of sixth-placed Cambridge United on Tuesday.

The Owls, who were relegated last season in record time after a desperate 2025-26 that was beset by financial problems, fan protests and an 18-point penalty, are currently eighth in the table, two points outside the play-off places after 11 games.

In a statement, Wednesday said Pedersen had provided "stability and leadership" during an "exceptional period in the club's history".

Sporting director Simon Wilson said the club had expected the start of the season to be "difficult" but offer "a recognisable style of play and greater consistency in our performances".

"Although we have accumulated points, we haven't seen enough progress in those areas," added , external Wilson.

"We believe making a change now gives us the best opportunity to establish those foundations and build towards the second half of the season and beyond."

Dane Pedersen also oversaw a 2-0 defeat at Notts County on Tuesday as part of a run of one win in six league matches, with Wednesday failing to score in four of those games.

Speaking after the defeat by Doncaster, Pedersen said he had heard chants directed against him by fans.

"I'm hurting like they are hurt," Pedersen told BBC Radio Sheffield.

"After zero points from two games, I'm not happy... nobody is happy.

"I'm sure we can bounce back and have a strong season."

'Wednesday can't keep playing this poorly'

Has Pedersen got the most difficult job in English football?

Troubled Sheff Wed appoint Pedersen as manager

Pederson, who had been predecessor Danny Rohl's assistant, signed a two-year contract to take over following the German's exit by mutual consent 12 days before the start of last season.

The Owls suffered the earliest relegation in EFL history in Pedersen's first campaign in charge in a chaotic season that saw fans boycotting matches and protests against then owner Dejphon Chansiri's running of the club that brought administration and an eventual 18-point penalty.

A 2-1 home win over West Bromwich Albion on the final day of last season was Wednesday's first in all competitions for seventh months as they finished with two victories, 32 defeats and a goal difference of -60 in the Championship.

Chansiri's reign officially ended in May with the takeover of the club by US consortium Arise Capital Partners.

Pedersen won four of his first five league matches this season including a 7-2 home victory over Bromley, but Wednesday's untimely loss of momentum has seen them slip out of the top six and cost Pedersen his job.

Follow Sheffield Wednesday on BBC Sounds

Pre-match, post-match and topical Owls content

'The writing was on the wall' - Analysis

The writing was on the wall once the fans turned at Notts County and Doncaster Rovers. Repeated chants of 'We want Henrik out' rang around the stadium.

Saturday could not have gone much worse for Pedersen.

The Owls boss switched to a 3-5-2 formation, which raised eyebrows. It wasn't so much the change of shape as the personnel being used.

Kieran Morrison is clearly a talented attacking winger. That's why he's on the books with Liverpool. Yet nobody who's watched him would say he's strong defensively at this stage in his career.

Yet here he was being asked to play as a left wing-back - a totally unnatural fit.

You can sort of understand why Wednesday wanted to give it a go. Morrison's attacking skill at least gave the Owls a chance to hurt Doncaster if he could get forward.

It didn't work at all. After just 20 minutes they were 2-0 down and Pedersen had already bailed on the idea, returning to a back four.

It was an awful look to make such a bold tactical call and be forced to abandon it before a quarter of the game had passed.

Wednesday were limp and lifeless in the first half. We've seen this too often — against Doncaster, Notts County, Huddersfield and Stockport. I would also include Salford in the EFL Trophy. Yes, Wednesday made some changes. Salford made eleven. And the Owls didn't lay a glove on them in the first 45 minutes.

That Wednesday were capable of creating the chances they did in the second half on Saturday almost makes it worse. They have the talent to turn it on. So why, too often, do they find it so hard to play well from the start?

The club's new owners wanted to give Pedersen a chance. They did — but have acted decisively in opting to make a change.

Now their challenge is to get their first appointment right.

articles.title: Íñigo Pérez firmó en Mestalla su centenario en Primera con tan sólo 38 años
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Villarreal se convierte en uno de los técnicos más jóvenes en alcanzar dicha cifra
articles.summary: El técnico del Villarreal se convierte en uno de los técnicos más jóvenes en alcanzar dicha cifra
articles.body: Íñigo Pérez celebró en Mestalla una cifra redonda y lo hizo con una importante victoria para su equipo. El técnico del Villarreal alcanzó los 100 partidos dirigidos en Primera División con el triunfo por 1-2 ante el Valencia, un resultado de peso para el conjunto amarillo y un hito en la todavía joven carrera del técnico navarro. Con tan sólo 38 años su precoz carrera le convierte en uno de los técnicos más jóvenes en alcanzar el triple dígito en el banquillo. Con el conjunto castellonense este fin de semana dirigió su décimo partido liguero, toda vez que la mayor parte de su carrera ha tenido lugar en Vallecas y al frente del Rayo. Una historia ue comenzó en febrero de 2024, cuando asumió las riendas del Rayo Vallecano tras la destitución de Francisco Rodríguez. Tras salvar a los madrileños en su primer curso, el salto de calidad llegó en las dos temporadas siguientes. El técnico navarro condujo al conjunto franjirrojo hasta la octava posición en ambas campañas, resultados que devolvieron al Rayo al panorama europeo y le permitieron disputar la Conference League. En su estreno continental, el equipo madrileño alcanzó la final, en la que cayó por 1-0 ante el Crystal Palace en Leipzig. De esta forma, el técnico suma 100 encuentros ligueros en Primera y un balance de 31 victorias, 35 empates y 34 derrotas, después de añadir el triunfo de Mestalla a los 99 partidos que acumulaba antes de la jornada. Y lo hace con tan sólo 38 años, 9 meses y 6 días. Una cifra que le convierte en uno de los más precoces a la hora de alcanzar dicha cifra. En comparación a los técnicos más laureados en la época reciente en la competición nacional ,supera entre otros a Pep Guardiola, que alcanzó los 100 partidos con 40 años, 1 mes y 2 días. O a Rafa Benítez , quien alcanzó el centenario con 42 años, 4 meses y 16 días. Por su parte Luis Enrique lo logró con 45 años, 9 meses y 9 días En eses sentido uno de los pocos que mejora la edad del técnico amarillo en cuanto a juventud se refiere para llegara este punto de su carrera, es otro ex del Villarreal como Unai Emery. El vasco firmó su centenario particular con con 38 años, 3 meses y 25 días.

articles.title: Alistair Johnston felt something again, says Celtic manager Martin O'Neill after injury in win at Hibs
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill explained Alistair Johnston "felt something again" after his substitute appearance in the win over Hibernian was cut short.
articles.body:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill explained Alistair Johnston "felt something again" after his substitute appearance in the win over Hibernian was cut short.

The Canada right-back, 28, missed most of last season with hamstring issues and had been absent since early August with a recurrence of the injury.

His appearance off the bench at Easter Road in Celtic's 2-1 victory lasted 21 minutes.

"We're not sure just at this moment," O'Neill told BBC Scotland.

"When you've had a couple of hamstring problems, I think that your concern is anything you might feel is a bit of a niggle.

"I don't know. He's not sure, neither is the doctor at this minute. He'll obviously need a scan and we'll see how he is."

More positively for O'Neill, central defender Cameron Carter-Vickers came through the final 17 minutes after taking over from Johnston. The United States defender had been missing since mid-September.

"Of course, we need every single body back," O'Neill said.

"He seems to have come through the game OK. Delighted that the big players are back."

Celtic restore four-point lead with narrow win at Hibs

Visit our Celtic page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

'In the circumstances, best win of season'

Camilo Duran's winner followed Jason Kerr's own leveller as Celtic bounced back from Thursday's 2-1 home Europa League defeat by Celta Vigo.

A ninth Scottish Premiership win out of 10, victory at Easter Road restored Celtic's four-point lead at the top of the division. Dundee United visit Celtic Park on Wednesday, with three more fixtures to come before the next international break.

"Absolutely delighted with it," O'Neill said.

"Considering the circumstances, considering the conditions today and considering what has happened on Thursday [losing to Celta Vigo], I thought this was our best win of the season and we didn't play particularly well in the game. It was even better than last Sunday.

"Thankfully, we did score so quickly afterwards [the Hibs goal] and we got the winning goal. It's a difficult afternoon even in good conditions form. I always find Easter Road really difficult."

articles.title: Bordalás, hundido: "Hemos tocado fondo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico getafense se mostró muy tocado tras una nueva goleada en contra
articles.summary: El técnico getafense se mostró muy tocado tras una nueva goleada en contra
articles.body: José Bordalás atendió a DAZN tras la goleada sufrida en San Mamés (4-0) ante el Athletic que cierra así una semana nefasta que se salda con nueve goles encajados en los últimos dos partidos y que en LaLiga le deja al borde del descenso. Palabras de Soria: “Respeto su opinión, es el capitán. Nos han hecho tres goles a balón parado, otro en un saque de banda… no nos lo podemos permitir. Hay que hacer una reflexión profunda”. Por qué: “La prueba es evidente, nos falta mucha consistencia, mis equipos siempre han sido solidarios y muy fuertes y estamos atravesando un momento de mucha fragilidad”. Roja a Mario Martín: “Prefiero no opinar, al final mi opinión no cambia nada. No podemos justificarnos ni protegernos en una excusa. La derrota ha sido clara y contundente”. Calmado: “Tenemos que pasar página rápido, pensar en el próximo compromiso, cambiar y corregir estos errores que nos están costando goles y derrotas. Mi opinión y lo que pensamos y lo que sentimos es que hemos tocado fondo y hay que cambiar rápidamente”. Vestuario: “Estamos dolidos, los jugadores lo están, sabemos que no hemos dado una buena imagen, es algo que debemos corregir y no nos podemos permitir”. Luis Milla y Arambarri: “No es momento, eran dos jugadores muy importantes. Y muchos otros que han salido. Ahora tenemos los jugadores que tenemos, no podemos pensar en los que no están, reflexionar y cambiar la imagen del equipo y volver a competir y volver a encontrar solidez que de alguna manera hemos perdido”. Sangría goleadora: “Lo he comentado, tres goles a balón parado, eso no lo podemos permitir. Si te meten tres goles a balón parado es que hay falta de atención, de responsabilidad y no podemos permitirlo. Mis equipos han destacado por ser muy fiables a nivel defensivo y no está ocurriendo. Hemos tocado de alguna manera fondo y tenemos que darle la vuelta a esta situación”.

articles.title: Dave Aranda Fired by Baylor, Latest Contract Buyout Info & Top HC Replacements After Loss to Kansas
articles.summary: Baylor's loss to Kansas on Saturday reportedly was the last straw for Dave Aranda's tenure as the program's head coach.
articles.body:
Baylor's loss to Kansas on Saturday reportedly was the last straw for Dave Aranda's tenure as the program's head coach.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Sunday that Baylor fired Aranda during his seventh season at the helm. The Bears fell to 4-3 with Saturday's 25-24 defeat, which ended with the Jayhawks blocking a field goal in the final seconds and then kneeling it out.

Baylor defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will be the interim for the program that is also facing a hefty buyout:

Here is a look at some potential replacement candidates:

Baylor is now left looking at replacements despite what was such a promising start to Aranda's time as the head coach.

While the Bears were just 2-7 during his first season in 2020, they made a massive leap in his second season by going 12-2 and winning the Sugar Bowl over Ole Miss. It seemed to be an announcement that Baylor would be a national factor under its new head coach.

However, things never returned to that level.

Baylor went a combined 22-28 the next four seasons and didn't finish with more than eight wins in any of those campaigns.

There was renewed hope for the 2026 season when Aranda landed Florida transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, but that optimism faded with a 17-16 loss to Auburn in the opener. Offense was also a major problem in a 17-6 loss to TCU.

Lagway has completed just 52.1 percent of his passes, and the Bears are now in a position where they are largely playing out the string of the season following a 4-3 start. It would take a dramatic turnaround for them to be considered even a darkhorse challenger for the College Football Playoff.

As for the potential replacements, a focus on the state of Texas would make sense.

Baylor could offer North Texas head coach Neal Brown, UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor and Houston offensive coordinator Slade Nagle an opportunity to take the next step in their careers while remaining in the state they are familiar with from a recruiting and playing standpoint.

Recruiting the state of Texas well would raise the ceiling for the Bears, especially since so many of their Big 12 rivals are in the state.

Jason Eck is also a rising coach who could find himself landing a number of offers this offseason as he continues to find success at New Mexico. Perhaps moving on from Aranda early will give Baylor an early start in the pursuit before other high-profile programs move on from their head coach.

For now, though, the Bears will turn their attention to Friday's game against UCF following a coaching change.

articles.title: El Bournemouth le saca los colores a un Manchester United que entra en números rojos
articles.standfirst: La abultada derrota contra los 'cherries' les sumerge en su peor inicio de la era Premier tras ocho jornadas disputadas
articles.summary: La abultada derrota contra los 'cherries' les sumerge en su peor inicio de la era Premier tras ocho jornadas disputadas
articles.body: El efecto que supuso la llegada de Michael Carrick al banquillo de Old Trafford mediada la temporada pasada ha quedado completamente difuminado. Los 'red devils' enlazan ocho partidos sin ganar entre todas las competiciones y la abultada derrota contra el Bournemouth (0-3) les ha sumergido en su peor inicio tras ocho jornadas en la era Premier. Al igual que sucedió con Lisandro, que volvió a arrancar como suplente, Carrick sentó a una institución como Bruno Fernandes tras las palabras pronunciadas después de la derrota contra el Como en Champions. Su lugar, como falso extremo izquierdo, lo ocupó Mason Mount. Otro de los que se cayó después de 'naufragar' en el Sinigaglia fue De Ligt. El Bournemouth salió con el cuchillo entre los dientes. En los primeros compases, se reclamó un penalti por mano de Dalot y, poco después, Lenny Yoro evitó que Evanilson empujase sobre la línea. Los 'cherries' estaban encontrando una autopista por ambos costados del Manchester United. Poco a poco, lograron sofocar la intensidad con la que se había plantado el Bournemouth en Old Trafford. En el 37', sin embargo, Rayan 'empaló' de primeras libre de marca en el segundo palo una falta lateral servida por Kluivert. 'Colapsó' el Manchester United y, en el 43', Truffert le comió la tostada a Lenny Yoro para asistir a Tavernier. De inmediato, se desplegó una pancarta en uno de los fondos donde podía leerse 'standars' (estándares). La cara de Carrick y Berrada era un poema. Con un único remate a puerta en toda la primera parte que Petrovic mandó a córner, Carrick estaba obligado a reaccionar... y dio entrada a Cunha por Tielemans al descanso. Ahora bien, no se había cumplido ni un minuto cuando Evanilson anotó el 0-3 tras un error en salida de Heaven, que ya había provocado la falta del primer gol. El linier, sin embargo, levantó la bandera. El excanterano del Arsenal, que poco después cometió otro error mal resuelto por Rayan, estaba haciendo aguas. No le quedó más remedio a Carrick que retirarlo. Lisandro, ausente desde su 'rajada' en el Metropolitano, fue su reemplazo. Rayan, mientras, volvió a perdonar desde dentro del área con un disparo que cruzó en exceso para sortear a Lammens. Estaba mucho más cerca el 0-3 que el gol que le permitiese meterse en el partido al Manchester United... y así acabó siendo. Lewis Cook recogió un balón dividido en el centro del campo y metió un pase en profundidad resuelto por Evanilson de manera impecable tras sortear la salida de Lammens. El fallo de comunicación del belga con Lisandro y Maguire fue dantesco. Todavía quedaban 20' para finalizar el partido. Pero la gente comenzó a desfilar de Old Trafford... mientras que Bruno Fernandes dejó de calentar para sentarse en el banquillo. Zirkzee y Lacey entraron por delante del luso. La situación, desde luego, es absolutamente dramática en un Manchester United que podría cerrar la jornada en descenso si el Sunderland le gana al Leeds.

articles.title: Iraola frena el ascenso del Brighton y celebra su primera victoria en Anfield
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Wirtz, con ayuda de Gross, e Isak en la primera parte impulsan el triunfo del Liverpool
articles.summary: Los goles de Wirtz, con ayuda de Gross, e Isak en la primera parte impulsan el triunfo del Liverpool
articles.body: Iraola ya se había estrenado en Champions y Carabao Cup. En Premier, sin embargo, todavía se le resistía su primera victoria en Anfield a los mandos de su nuevo Liverpool. Más pronto que tarde tenía que llegar... y fue para frenar el ascenso de un Brighton (2-0) que enlazaba cuatro triunfos consecutivos en la competición doméstica. Iraola, un día más, ubicó a Ronald Araújo en el lateral derecho del Liverpool. Por delante, en la posición de extremo, no tuvo a Víctor Muñoz o Ngumoha... sino Barcola. Fue Gakpo quien se acomodó en izquierda. El Brighton, por su parte, se plantó en Anfield con el que, perfectamente, podría ser considerado su once de gala... con Chema Andrés asentado en el doble pivote junto a Gross. El Brighton, a pesar de la temprana lesión de Kadioglu, saltó a Anfield con la personalidad que le ha convertido en el equipo revelación de la Premier en este primer tramo de temporada. Con Chema Andrés retrasando su posición entre centrales para poder ver el campo de cara, le invitó al Liverpool a que saltase a 'morder'. Antes del primer cuarto de hora, tras una excelente combinación por derecha, Ayari mandó por encima del larguero un remate desde dentro del área con Alisson vendido. Le valió al Liverpool para despertar. Tanto es así, instantes después, logró inclinar el marcador en una acción que nació de un saque de banda a favor. Estuvo 'vivo' Araújo para ganar el duelo por el sector derecho y servir un servicio atrás que, con ayuda de Gross en su intento por despejar, Florian Wirtz mandó a guardar. Primer gol del curso para el ex del Leverkusen, que viene creciendo en las últimas semanas. El tanto, desde luego, reforzó la moral del Liverpool. Asfixiaron al Brighton desde la presión y, tras una mano providencial de Verbruggen a disparo cruzado de Gakpo, Isak fue el encargado de duplicar la ventaja a pase de un Barcola que 'devoró' a Boscagli. Sexta 'diana' en esta Premier para el fichaje más caro en la historia del conjunto 'red'. El ritmo, a decir verdad, era difícilmente para un Liverpool que, eso sí, logró evitar que el Brighton recortase diferencias antes de poner dirección a vestuarios. Jacquet y Araújo pusieron la cara para bloquear dos disparos y, tras un robo alto de Chema Andrés, Ayari mandó un disparo lejano a la madera. La lesión de Chema Andrés durante los primeros compases del segundo tiempo supuso un contratiempo para el Brighton. Hürzeler tuvo que retrasar la posición de Ayari para situar a Yalcouyé por detrás de Kostoulas. También se marchó tocado Wirtz, ovacionado por Anfield, pocos minutos después. No bajó los brazos el Brighton en busca del gol que le permitiese meterse de lleno en el partido. La realidad, sin embargo, es que Alisson no tuvo que realizar ni una intervención durante todo el segundo acto. El Liverpool, con un Araújo imperial, cerro filas y, por tercera vez esta temporada, dejó su portería a cero para asaltar los puestos Champions donde, eso sí, todavía se mantienen los 'seagulls'.

articles.title: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton player rater: Isak, Barcola and Wirtz turn up
articles.summary: How Liverpool and Brighton's players rated following their Premier League match.
articles.body:
Liverpool beat Brighton 2-0 at Anfield with Alexander Isak scoring the second goal, four minutes after Pascal Gross' own-goal gave the home side the lead.

Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Alisson: Didn't have a save to make in the first half but was nearly punished when Yasin Ayari hit the post after his careless pass out from the back. Will be delighted with the clean sheet. 7

Ronald Araujo: Showed great strength in the build-up for the first goal and was solid again, defensively. Nearly scored too but his effort was saved. 7

Jeremy Jacquet: Another good performance. Composed on the ball and made some crucial blocks. 7

Virgil van Dijk: Back to his usual self after a relatively poor display midweek. Another clean sheet in the Premier League. 7

Milos Kerkez: Didn't have the best of games and had his work cut out against Diego Gomez but ultimately, part of a Liverpool backline that kept Brighton out. 6

Ryan Gravenberch: Solid work rate, particularly in a game where Liverpool had a lot less of the ball. 7

Alexis Mac Allister: Certainly one of Liverpool 's better players this season and bar some loose passes, this was another encouraging display from the Argentine. 7

Bradley Barcola: Did superbly to tee up Isak and was a handful all afternoon for Olivier Boscagli. Did everything but score. 8

Florian Wirtz: Played with such a confidence and unfortunate that his strike was an own-goal from Gross. Caused Brighton plenty of problems throughout. Went off shortly after receiving treatment. 8

Cody Gakpo: Constantly threatened, playing down his preferred left, and had two efforts saved. Unlucky not to get an assist too. 7

Alexander Isak: A simple finish but in the right place at the right time for his sixth Premier League goal in as many games. Still not at his best yet but with those numbers, Andoni Iraola will be delighted. 7

Nyoni (on 65, Wirtz): Solid challenge instantly after coming on and the teenager looks like he is improving every week. 7

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Gomez, Endo, Chiesa, McConnell.

Bart Verbruggen: Made some good saves in the first half but was undone by the deflection for the first goal and had no chance for Isak's strike. 5

Ferdi Kadioglu: Forced off with an injury in the sixth minute. Was holding his hip as he came off. 5

Luka Vuskovic: Part of a back line that conceded in the league for the first time since 16 September, but the 19-year-old looked good on the ball. 6

Lewis Dunk: Like Vuskovic, battled well but the Brighton back line were punished by Liverpool 's ruthlessness. 5

Olivier Boscagli: Lost the ball for Liverpool 's second goal and struggled to deal with Barcola. Booked for a foul on Barcola just before half-time and replaced at the break. 4

Pascal Gross: Should have got an assist when he teed up Ayari but did not cover himself in glory when his clearance landed at Wirtz's feet and the subsequent strike deflected off Gross and ended up in the back of the net. 5

Chema Andres: Was good on the ball and tidy in possession but took a knock and was replaced early on in the second half. 6

Diego Gomez: Played a lovely through-ball to Gross for Ayari's chance and linked up really well with Joao Costinha. 7

Yasin Ayari: Missed a huge chance when the game was 0-0 and his side were punished shortly after, then hit the post with a good effort in the first half. 6

Maxim De Cuyper: Had a quiet first half and dropped into left-back for the second half after Jack Hinshelwood came on for Boscagli. 5

Charalampos Kostoulas: Got on the ball plenty and always offered an option but did not do enough to truly threaten Alisson. 6

Costinha (on 6, Kadioglu): Thrown in early on and linked well with Gomez going forward but struggled to contain Gakpo. 6

Hinshelwood (on 46, Boscagli): Did well after coming on but could not get Brighton back in the game. 6

Yalcouye (on 54, Andres): Did not get on the ball enough after coming on. 5

Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Rutter, David, Osman, O'Riley.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Man Utd 0-3 Bournemouth: Michael Carrick drops Bruno Fernandes but sees Cherries humble United at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Match report and free highlights as Manchester United were beaten 3-0 by  Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on Michael Carrick. The United boss dropped captain Bruno Fernandes and has now gone eight games without a win…
articles.body:
The 4-1 loss away to Como on Wednesday, a seventh game without a win, had already heaped pressure on Carrick with the issues exacerbated by the comments made by Fernandes that Gary Neville viewed as "a direct attack on the manager" and his tactics.

The United boss desperately needed a response. What he received from his confidence-shot players was a lacklustre display from the outset, Bournemouth deserving of their lead long before Rayan calmly volleyed in at the far post from Justin Kluivert's free-kick.

Ayden Heaven's wild lunge conceded that free-kick and it was Leny Yoro's slip that allowed Marcus Tavernier to slot in a second before the break, sparking boos from the home fans and further chants of 'sacked in the morning' from the jubilant away support.

Carrick turned to Matheus Cunha rather than Fernandes at half-time, hooking the desperately poor Youri Tielemans, but United got worse. Evanilson had one effort ruled out after calamitous defending. Rayan should have punished another bad Heaven mistake.

The arrival of Lisandro Martinez in place of the young defender did not improve things with a hapless cameo during which Evanilson beat Senne Lammens to the ball and finished fantastically for the third. Fernandes stayed on the bench. But what now?

For Marco Rose's Bournemouth, it is back-to-back wins and four in a row in all competitions. How long it remains Carrick's United is unclear. Eight games without a win, 16th in the table and one point above the drop zone, this is a team disjointed, a club divided.

The fans in the Stretford End directed their ire at the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox, singing Carrick's name as he walked down the tunnel before booing the players. And it is the manager whose job is now on the line. Only at Manchester United.

articles.title: Next Man United manager: Who could replace Michael Carrick?
articles.summary: Carrick is under huge pressure heading as Sunday’s home defeat to Bournemouth extended United’s winless run to eight games in all competitions
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is running out of time to save his job at Manchester United , with the club poised to ramp up the search for a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos took over football operations.

Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has come under huge pressure following United's worst start to a season in 40 years .

That pressure has only intensified after a dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night was followed by a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at home on Sunday, with fans streaming out of Old Trafford in their droves during the second half.

While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – Carrick's appears to be on the brink following criticism of his tactics by the United captain Bruno Fernandes , who was then left on the bench against Bournemouth.

While Carrick remained in charge for Sunday's defeat to the Cherries , the club have already discussed potential replacements should he follow the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim under the Ineos leadership.

Carrick spoke for almost six minutes at the start of his pre-match press conference on Friday, imploring the importance of "sacrifice", "humility" and "hard work" in an impassioned speech which highlighted the "values" of the club and "respecting" the responsibility of representing United.

But who could United turn to as they seek to salvage their campaign?

The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer . Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. The 48-year-old remains highly regarded in English football after taking over a Newcastle side in the relegation zone and leading them to the club's highest Premier League finish in two decades, as well as their first domestic silverware in 70 years. Howe twice took Newcastle into the Champions League playing an energetic, high-intensity style of football that would be popular at Old Trafford. He is currently the favourite with the bookies.

Brighton have been the surprise package in the Premier League this season and the 33-year-old Hurzeler has drawn praise for turning the Seagulls into a side capable of competing with the country's biggest clubs. Brighton's 3-0 victory over champions Arsenal earlier this season was a masterclass in modern coaching while Hurzeler's side also knocked United out of the Carabao Cup with a brilliant 3-2 win at Old Trafford. The Independent's Chief Football Writer Miguel Delaney has reported that Hurzeler is admired at Old Trafford but Brighton would demand significant compensation for the highly-rated German and United may not have the cash. At Brighton, Hurzeler has also enjoyed an environment where the club have made all the right decisions off the pitch. At United, he would arguably be walking into the opposite.

The Brighton boss said on Friday : "I'm fully focused on my job here. I've got no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick and the job he has done at Manchester United the last season. He's a great human being, a great personality, and I really respect him. There's nothing more to say about that. I'm really privileged to be here. I'm part of a journey [at Brighton] and I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey... "We have built this [together] over the years. We've had good periods, we've had bad periods. To build these connections you need time. You don't take these things for granted. It's a people business. Making a people business out of this pressure business is something I don't take for granted and something I won't throw away that fast."

The former wunderkind of German coaching was reportedly on United's radar when they sacked Ruben Amorim at the start of the year, but as an option for the summer following the World Cup. Well, that was a bit of a disaster for the former Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig coach, as Germany were knocked out in the last-32 by Paraguay. Nagelsmann, 39, would naturally be interested in managing United and the club's director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, previously worked with him at Red Bull.

The Spaniard has done a superb job at Aston Villa by securing Champions League qualification and ending the club's trophy drought with victory in the Europa League. But Aston Villa will be even more determined to keep Emery given the club are only in the early stages of their rebuild under him, having completely overhauled the spine of their team over the summer. As it is, Emery enjoys complete control over his project at Villa Park, a reality he is unlikely to find at Old Trafford, while he appears enthused by the challenge of constructing a second competitive team in the Premier League. With Emery, who is under contract until 2029, United would also need to pay Villa compensation, and that may place him above their budget.

The appeal of the combustible Italian only has grown while United have been accused of becoming too passive and pedestrian on the pitch. Conte is one of the most demanding coaches in the game and would instantly bring a level of intensity and urgency that has been lacking this season, while his CV – with Serie A titles at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli and a Premier League crown with Chelsea – commands respect. Conte also brought an immediate improvement when he took charge of a floundering Tottenham five years ago and led them back into the Champions League, which now has to be United's biggest concern. So the 57-year-old offers impact, but then what? Conte has a sharp tongue and is not afraid to criticise his bosses if he feels they are failing to support him. His exit from Tottenham in March 2023 followed a stunning evisceration of the club in a now legendary press conference at Southampton. United would be playing with fire but options of Conte's calibre are few and far between.

In a statement on Friday, Conte distanced himself from the Manchester United job while branding reports that he is in "advanced negotiations" with any club as "speculation". He said: "Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right. I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my 'strong personality'. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments."

The former Arsenal, Barcelona and Chelsea midfielder is developing a reputation as Europe's brightest young coach – as his brilliant Como side demonstrated by thrashing United in the Champions League on Wednesday night. The Spaniard appears committed to his project in northern Italy, though, and also has a financial incentive to continue leading Como in their debut Champions League campaign due to owning a stake in the Serie A club. The 39-year-old's own stock is also rising and the lure of returning to one of his former clubs in the future, such as Barcelona, could result in Fabregas taking a patient and considered approach to his next move.

Well, we've been here before. Before Michael Carrick stepped into the breach in January it was Under-18s manager Darren Fletcher, who oversaw the draw with Burnley and FA Cup third-round defeat to Brighton. Before him, Ruud van Nistelrooy held the reins between Erik ten Hag's dismissal and Amorim's appointment and before that, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer experienced the same cycle of boom-and-bust that Carrick has gone through over the past 10 months. In short, there's no shortage of former United players who are available to remind an underperforming dressing room of the importance of the badge and the meaning of the shirt. It could be time for Fletcher to give Sir Alex another call.

articles.standfirst: El noruego entró muy bien ante el Deportivo y aumenta las alternativas de Simeone
articles.summary: El noruego entró muy bien ante el Deportivo y aumenta las alternativas de Simeone
articles.body: Comenzó la temporada Simeone sin delanteros. Con Sorloth lesionado, Julián metido en su culebrón veraniego y Jonathan David en Turín. Los rojiblancos iniciaron el curso teniendo que reinventarse en ataque para las primeras jornadas. Ahora, una vez se han cumplido diez fechas del campeonato, el Cholo empieza a ver la luz en la parcela ofensiva. Julián ha roto su sequía, Jonathan David se ha acoplado a la perfección y ahora, Sorloth se suma a la pelea. El noruego, que se lesionó en sus primeros días de pretemporada y estuvo varias semanas fuera de combate, apareció en el segundo acto ante el Deportivo con una gran actuación. El de Trondheim entró en el minuto 67 en lugar de Kang-in y entendió a la perfección lo que necesitaba el equipo. Se hizo fuerte en los balones aéreos dando salida a los rojiblancos, ganó varias pelotas al espacio… En definitiva, unos minutos que le pueden servir para encontrar su mejor versión. Sorloth, que suma 44 goles como rojiblanco en sus dos temporadas, llega en el momento clave. Simeone tiene a sus tres delanteros enchufados justo antes de visitar al Levante y recibir a Bayern y Barcelona. El noruego tan solo ha disputado 43 minutos en este curso. 40 en LaLiga y tres en Champions. En Vitoria no estuvo del todo cómodo pero ante el Deportivo encontró una buena versión. Su entrada al campo ayudó a los del Cholo en el tramo final. Ahora, con la lesión olvidada, pretende mejorar sus números de la pasada temporada donde se quedó en 13 goles en Liga. En el curso anterior, el primero como rojiblanco, llegó a la veintena de tantos en el campeonato liguero. Si sus cifras se acercan a las de la 24/25 será una gran noticia para Simeone que por fin cuenta con sus tres atacantes en plenitud. La irrupción de Sorloth coincide con el momento de la redención de Julián.

articles.body:
Liverpool 2-0 Brighton: Reds Secure First Home Premier League Win

Liverpool secured their first home victory of the Premier League season with a convincing 2-0 win over Brighton at Anfield, producing a decisive first half performance to overcome one of the division's most in form sides.

Two goals in four minutes put Liverpool firmly in control, with Pascal Groß's own goal opening the scoring before Alexander Isak doubled the advantage. Brighton had opportunities to make life uncomfortable for the hosts, yet Liverpool took their chances when they mattered and managed the game effectively thereafter.

The result lifted Liverpool from fifth to fourth in the Premier League table, leaving them one point behind third placed Brighton, whose impressive run suffered only its second defeat in 13 matches across all competitions this season.

Pascal Groß Own Goal Gives Liverpool the Lead

Brighton began with intent and created a promising opportunity before Liverpool found their rhythm. Yasin Ayari was presented with a chance following an excellent attacking move, but his effort sailed over the crossbar. It was a costly miss for the visitors, who would soon find themselves chasing the game.

Liverpool took the lead in the 17th minute through an unfortunate intervention from Groß. Florian Wirtz attempted a shot that appeared to be drifting wide, only for the Brighton midfielder to divert the ball into his own net.

The goal ended Brighton's run of defensive resilience in the Premier League, following their 1-1 draw against Leeds on 5 September. For Liverpool, it provided an important platform to build on, with the home crowd sensing an opportunity to see their side take control.

Alexander Isak Extends Liverpool's Advantage

Liverpool struck again just four minutes later, with Isak finishing a well constructed attack to make it 2-0.

Bradley Barcola was instrumental in the move, showing excellent pace and skill down the right flank before delivering a dangerous cross into the penalty area. Isak met the delivery with a controlled volley, giving Brighton goalkeeper little chance and continuing his impressive scoring form.

The goal marked Isak's third consecutive Premier League appearance with a goal, underlining his growing influence in Liverpool's attack. His finishing provided the cutting edge required to turn a promising performance into a commanding position.

Liverpool's ability to punish Brighton during a brief spell of defensive uncertainty ultimately proved decisive. The visitors had started positively, but the two goals forced them to rethink their approach.

Brighton Threaten as Liverpool Hold Firm

Brighton were handed a potential route back into the contest when Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson lost possession while attempting to play out from the back. Ayari seized the opportunity, but his effort struck the foot of the right hand post.

It was a significant let off for Liverpool, who could have faced a far more demanding second half had Brighton converted. Instead, the Reds maintained their advantage and saw out the match without allowing the visitors to turn their possession into a sustained comeback.

The victory also continued Liverpool's encouraging run at Anfield under head coach Andoni Iraola, following two home Champions League wins and a Carabao Cup victory.

For Liverpool, the three points represent an important step in their Premier League campaign. Brighton remain third despite the defeat, while Liverpool move into fourth, just one point behind their opponents.

Liverpool will take confidence from a performance built on clinical finishing, attacking quality and defensive resilience when it mattered most.

articles.title: Man Utd 0 Bournemouth 3 - how the players rated
articles.summary: Another catastrophic day for Manchester United and a glorious one for Bournemouth - how did the players rate?
articles.body:
Another desperate day for Manchester United as Bournemouth win at Old Trafford for the third time in four years.

United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench by manager Michael Carrick and stayed there as the Cherries comfortably won 3-0.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Senne Lammens: Another of those games where everything is looking solid - until it isn't. Massive error for Bournemouth 's third goal. 4

Leny Yoro: Vital clearance to deny Evanilson a tap-in. Had situation under control but then slipped to gift Bournemouth their second. 5

Harry Maguire: Regained the captain's armband taken off him by Erik ten Hag. Blocked early Rayan chance and surged forward to try and create at the other end. 6

Ayden Heaven (off 64, Martinez): Some good moments and lots of promise but plenty being asked of the 20-year-old. Yellow card for jumping into a tackle Evanilson jumped out of the way of. Proved to be costly with the resulting free-kick leading to Bournemouth 's opener. 5

Diogo Dalot: Got forward well but shooting erratic and pass straight to Evanilson inside own half didn't inspire confidence. Tried to rouse his team but didn't have a lot of success. 5

Carlos Baleba (off, 72, Zirkzee): Not scared to take a risk despite the pressure his team are playing under. Does give United drive in central areas. 5

Andrey Santos: Tielemans' poor control forced him into a rash tackle on Truffert that brought a yellow card. Not much of an impact. 4

Amad Diallo (off 78, Amad): Beautiful bit of skill took him past Truffert but seen too infrequently and passing not accurate enough. 4

Youri Tielemans (off 46, Cunha): Not secure enough in possession for the job Carrick wanted from him. Big disappointment. Off at half-time. 4

Mason Mount: Alternated positions with Tielemans and tried to get on the ball. Thought he was crossing for a team-mate and annoyed when no-one moved for it. 5

Bryan Mbeumo: Hardly in the game until released for shot late in first-half. Had another effort in second half. 6

Matheus Cunha (on 46, Tielemans): Introduced at half-time and did manage a curling effort from edge of the area, which was off target. 6

Lisandro Martinez (on 64, Heaven): Nearly gave away a third goal, and nearly scored one at the other end. 6

Joshua Zirkzee (on 72, Baleba): Not even a consolation goal today. 5

Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, De Ligt, Fernandes, T Fletcher.

Dorde Petrovic: Quiet game until called upon to turn away Mbeumo effort. 6

James Hill: Ambitious long ball to no-one, then crucial interception of Youri Tielemans' low cross before it reached Mbeumo. Solid when pressure mounted. 6

Adam Smith (off 87, Diakite): Man Utd didn't play with conventional wide player, but didn't get drawn out of position. Matched Diogo Dalot when he started running at him after half-time. 6

Antonio Silva: Cruised through the majority of the first half. Busier in the second but always had situation under control. 7

Adrien Truffert: Seized on Yoro error to create the visitors second. 7

Lewis Cook: Quietly effective. Read the game well and stepped in to make challenges and win the ball when required. 7

Tyler Adams: Booked for chopping down Tielemans and wrong side of Mbeumo when he went down but held sway in midfield duel. 7

Rayan: Found space around Dalot in the early stages but didn't make the most of it. Better delivery was nearly converted by Evanilson and superb first-time finish for opener. Should have had a second. 8

Marcus Tavernier (off 87, Adli): Got free on the left on a couple of occasions but couldn't pick out a team-mate with his cross. Easiest of finishes for Bournemouth 's second. 8

Justin Kluivert (off, Gannon-Doak, 62): Brilliant free-kick to create the opener. Another eye-catching display. 7

Evanilson (off 87, Kroupi): Close to opener with attempted diving header and did have a goal ruled out for offside. Brilliant finish for the third. 8

Ben Gannon-Doak (on 62, Kluivert): Settled in easily to game that was already set. 7

Ryan Christie (on 75, Cook): Easy game. 6

Subs not used: Di Gregorio, Soler, Brooks, Rodriguez.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Representative of Real Madrid star speaks out on player’s future amid exit links – “He needs to play”
articles.summary: After the worst possible start to the season, in which he struggled to get enough game-time under Jose Mourinho, Endrick is having a resurgence of sorts afte...
articles.body:
After the worst possible start to the season, in which he struggled to get enough game-time under Jose Mourinho, Endrick is having a resurgence of sorts after the international break.

The Brazilian played a crucial role in Real Madrid's comeback win over AS Roma in the Champions League and played 70 minutes in the 4-1 win over Sevilla.

Despite that, Endrick's future at Real Madrid remains uncertain , as there is no guarantee he will become a first-team regular anytime soon.

Endrick's future at Real Madrid is still uncertain. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images)

Michael Yormark, president of Roc Nation – the agency which represents Endrick, has opened up on the striker's situation, admitting that a January move cannot be ruled out if the minutes do not increase.

"His first option is to stay at Real Madrid, but he needs to play and we'll see how everything develops until the next transfer window in January," Yormark said (h/t Defensa Central ).

He went on to explain that conversations are ongoing, with Endrick keen to make the most of a career he knows is finite.

"The future of Endrick? It's a constantly evolving process, and we need to see how things develop between now and the end of 2026, before the winter transfer window opens. We recently met with Endrick in Madrid and had a great conversation.

"He's a very talented guy and eager to play, so we'll see what happens. He loves Madrid, the team he's on, and his teammates, but when you think about the length of his career… you realize it's short, and you want to make the most of it," he added.

What's in store for Endrick's future? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

The uncertainty surrounding his game time has inevitably alerted suitors, with Endrick's profile making him a hugely attractive proposition.

The Brazilian international has already been linked with a move for Italian giants AS Roma and AC Milan and it won't be surprising to see more clubs lining up for him as we move closer towards the January transfer window.

It is clear that Endrick needs regular elite-level football to continue his development, something he is unlikely to find at Real Madrid in the immediate future.

That reality is said to be making him seriously consider his options. The situation is nothing new, either, with Madrid having loaned him to Olympique Lyonnais in the second half of last season.

He stayed put in the summer at Mourinho's request, but the Portuguese has since struggled to carve out a role for him, even after his return from an early-season injury.

For now, the hope within his camp is that his recent contributions earn him greater involvement. Should that fail to materialise, though, a mid-season switch to a club offering guaranteed minutes may prove increasingly difficult to resist.

articles.title: Manchester United: Michael Carrick head coach on brink of losing job after Bournemouth defeat
articles.summary: Michael Carrick looks poised to lose his job as Manchester United head coach following their 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, according to Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher.
articles.body:
The humbling defeat leaves United just above the relegation zone following their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

"It is going to get ridiculously difficult for Michael Carrick to be Manchester United manager moving forward. That's the problem the club have got," said Neville during Sky Sports' match commentary.

Carrick struck a defiant tone after the game but his lengthy applause towards the United fans after the final whistle were immediately interpreted as a farewell gesture.

"Michael Carrick needs to be relieved of his duties tonight," added Jamie Carragher. "Not just for the good of Manchester United but also for the good of Michael Carrick.

"Manchester United need to make that decision tonight."

Carrick led United to Champions League football after taking over from Ruben Amorim in mid-season last year, but United are winless in their last eight matches amid a wretched start to the current campaign.

"I did think last season that the club should have gone for the best manager they could have got and not given the job to Michael Carrick because I felt this might happen. But this has gone very, very sour very quickly and the club is a mess," said Neville.

Carrick's name was chanted loudly by the Old Trafford faithful following Bournemouth's game-sealing third goal but Neville fears that time may already be up for his former team-mate.

"Carrick is popular. But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular. They have badly let the club down.

"Tomorrow, they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary.

"The Manchester United fans are singing Carrick's name because the reality tomorrow is: will he be the manager?

Bruno Fernandes was dropped from the match on Sunday after he criticised Carrick's tactics in the wake of Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League. Surprisingly, the United captain stayed on the bench for the entirety of the defeat to Bournemouth.

"Picking the team is always a difficult decision," Carrick told Sky Sports . "We've got to make what we feel is the right one for the team to try to get the performance we want."

Carrick described his reasons for dropping his captain as "pure football."
